posts.title: Dangote’s $16 Billion Kenya Refinery Project

posts.content:
Dangote has officially begun construction of a massive $16 billion oil refinery project in Kenya, representing a significant investment in Africa’s energy and industrial infrastructure. The project is expected to strengthen Kenya’s energy security, reduce dependence on imported refined petroleum products, and create substantial opportunities across construction, logistics, manufacturing, and related industries.

The development also highlights the growing scale of African-led private-sector investment in strategic infrastructure and energy. As one of Africa’s most prominent industrial groups, Dangote’s expansion reflects the increasing importance of large-scale projects in driving economic growth, employment, trade, and regional development.

With Kenya serving as an important gateway to East Africa, the refinery could have wider implications for regional energy supply chains and economic integration. Such projects can create opportunities for local businesses, international investors, technology providers, contractors, and service companies across the continent.

posts.title: Zambia’s Copper Boom: A New Era of Mining & Investment
posts.excerpt: Zambia is reaffirming its commitment to transforming its mining sector by aiming to triple annual copper production to 3 million tonnes, supported by more than US$10 billion in mining investments since 2021. As one of Africa’s richest copper-producing nations, Zambia is leveraging strong investor confidence, policy reforms, and strategic partnerships to unlock the full potential […]
posts.content:
Zambia is reaffirming its commitment to transforming its mining sector by aiming to triple annual copper production to 3 million tonnes, supported by more than US$10 billion in mining investments since 2021. As one of Africa’s richest copper-producing nations, Zambia is leveraging strong investor confidence, policy reforms, and strategic partnerships to unlock the full potential of its mineral resources.

Industry stakeholders are emphasizing the need for continued investment in mineral exploration, local processing facilities, transport infrastructure, renewable energy, and power generation to sustain long-term growth. Expanding domestic value addition and modernizing logistics will not only strengthen Zambia’s mining ecosystem but also increase export competitiveness and attract new global investors.

With the global shift toward electric vehicles, renewable energy, and advanced manufacturing driving unprecedented demand for copper, Zambia is uniquely positioned to become a key supplier of this critical mineral. The country’s ambitious mining strategy presents significant opportunities for businesses, investors, technology providers, and infrastructure developers across Africa and beyond.

posts.content:
Ethiopia is taking a transformative step toward becoming one of Africa’s leading aviation and logistics hubs with its ambitious US$12.5 billion Bishoftu International Airport project. The mega infrastructure development has already begun attracting global investors, financial institutions, and strategic partners, reflecting strong international confidence in Ethiopia’s long-term economic vision.

Designed to become one of Africa’s largest airports, the Bishoftu International Airport will dramatically increase passenger handling capacity while expanding cargo operations to support growing trade across Africa and beyond. The project is expected to strengthen Ethiopia’s position as a regional aviation gateway, improve supply chain connectivity, enhance tourism, facilitate international business, and generate substantial employment opportunities.

For businesses across Asia and Africa, the development presents significant opportunities in airport infrastructure, engineering, logistics, aviation services, construction, technology, hospitality, and foreign investment. It also reinforces Africa’s rapidly expanding infrastructure landscape and highlights the continent’s commitment to building world-class transport networks that support economic growth and regional integration.

posts.title: AACCI Director General M. J. Puri sets out vision for cross-continental growth
posts.excerpt: Trade and investment between Asia and Africa will depend increasingly on stronger local networks, clearer regulation and closer cooperation between business and government, according to M. J. Puri, Director General of the Asia Africa Chamber of Commerce and Industry. In a recent interview, Puri said the chamber’s purpose was rooted in long-term economic partnership. “AACCI […]
posts.content:
Trade and investment between Asia and Africa will depend increasingly on stronger local networks, clearer regulation and closer cooperation between business and government, according to M. J. Puri, Director General of the Asia Africa Chamber of Commerce and Industry.

In a recent interview, Puri said the chamber’s purpose was rooted in long-term economic partnership. “AACCI serves as a strategic bridge between Asia and Africa, fostering trade, investment, entrepreneurship, technology transfer, and institutional collaboration,” he explained. “Our mission is to create sustainable economic partnerships and strengthen South-South cooperation.”
That role is becoming more visible as businesses across Africa and Asia look for new markets, investment partners and supply chains. Puri said AACCI’s expansion strategy is being shaped by the need to work closer to the ground, particularly through national chapters that can connect local business communities with regional and international opportunities.

“Our growth is driven by the need for local engagement through country chapters that facilitate business networking, trade promotion, investment opportunities, and policy dialogue,” Puri told SiGMA News.

Through these country chapters, AACCI gives companies, chambers, investors and institutions a direct route into conversations that often stall because of distance, limited market knowledge or lack of trusted contacts.

Agriculture, energy and technology among priority sectors

Puri said the scope for cooperation is not confined to one industry, with opportunities spread across both established sectors and fast-growing digital fields.

“Agriculture, renewable energy, manufacturing, infrastructure, healthcare, tourism, education, fintech, AI, logistics, and digital transformation remain the strongest sectors for collaboration,” he said.

The list reflects the scale of economic overlap between the two regions. Many African economies are seeking investment in infrastructure, industrialisation, healthcare and digital services, while Asian companies are looking for new partnerships, production bases and growth markets. AACCI says its role is to bring those interests into a more structured framework.
The Director General also acknowledged that the opportunity is not without obstacles. “Information gaps, financing constraints, logistics challenges, regulatory complexity, and limited institutional connectivity,” he said, were among the main barriers limiting cooperation.

He said AACCI works to address those barriers “through partnerships and trade facilitation.”
Puri stressed that governments and businesses cannot build these links alone. “It is essential,” he said of cross-sector collaboration. “Governments, businesses, academia, and development institutions must work together to create sustainable economic growth.”

Startups and digital industries move into focus

AACCI is also looking closely at entrepreneurs, startups and emerging digital sectors. Puri said the chamber supports entrepreneurs “through networking, international exposure, investor access, mentorship, trade missions, and business development platforms.”
That support is likely to become more important as smaller companies and technology-led businesses seek access to investors and cross-border networks. Puri said gaming, entertainment and technology are becoming more important economic sectors.
“These sectors are becoming major economic contributors through innovation, digital transformation, job creation, and technology adoption,” he said.

He added that AACCI could help build responsible growth in these areas by bringing together different players. “AACCI can facilitate dialogue among investors, regulators, technology providers, and entrepreneurs to support responsible growth,” he argued.
Regulation, he suggested, will be central to whether fast-growing sectors can attract confidence and capital. “Transparency, compliance, and responsible governance are fundamental to sustainable industry growth and investor confidence,” he said.
Looking ahead, Puri said AACCI’s ambition is clear: “To become the leading Asia-Africa business bridge that drives trade, investment, entrepreneurship, and sustainable development across both continents.”

For AACCI, that means continuing to build platforms where business leaders, investors, entrepreneurs, chambers and institutions can meet, exchange ideas and turn regional potential into practical partnerships.

Source : Asia-Africa cooperation could unlock new gaming opportunities

posts.title: INDIA LAUNCHES MAJOR $51 BILLION MANUFACTURING DRIVE
posts.excerpt: India has launched a landmark US$51 billion manufacturing initiative aimed at transforming the country’s industrial landscape, reducing dependence on imports, and strengthening domestic production capabilities. The ambitious program focuses on expanding manufacturing capacity, modernizing industrial infrastructure, supporting MSMEs, and building resilient supply chains across key sectors. By encouraging innovation, advanced technologies, and greater private sector […]
posts.content:
India has launched a landmark US$51 billion manufacturing initiative aimed at transforming the country’s industrial landscape, reducing dependence on imports, and strengthening domestic production capabilities. The ambitious program focuses on expanding manufacturing capacity, modernizing industrial infrastructure, supporting MSMEs, and building resilient supply chains across key sectors. By encouraging innovation, advanced technologies, and greater private sector participation, the initiative is expected to create millions of employment opportunities while boosting productivity and long-term economic growth.

The manufacturing drive also reinforces India’s vision of becoming a global manufacturing and export powerhouse under the ‘Make in India’ strategy. With increased investment in strategic industries, the initiative is set to attract international manufacturers, enhance export competitiveness, and strengthen India’s role in global supply chains. The move is expected to open significant opportunities for businesses, investors, technology providers, and international trade partners across Asia, Africa, and other global markets, making it a major catalyst for industrial growth and cross-border economic cooperation.

posts.title: India–UK CETA Enters Into Force: A New Era of Trade & Economic Cooperation
posts.excerpt: The entry into force of the India–UK Comprehensive Economic & Trade Agreement (CETA) represents one of the most significant milestones in the economic partnership between India and the United Kingdom. Designed to strengthen bilateral trade and investment, the agreement provides greater market access, simplifies trade procedures, and supports long-term economic growth for both nations. CETA […]
posts.content:
The entry into force of the India–UK Comprehensive Economic & Trade Agreement (CETA) represents one of the most significant milestones in the economic partnership between India and the United Kingdom. Designed to strengthen bilateral trade and investment, the agreement provides greater market access, simplifies trade procedures, and supports long-term economic growth for both nations.

CETA is expected to create substantial opportunities for exporters, manufacturers, MSMEs, service providers, and investors by reducing trade barriers and encouraging cross-border business collaboration. Key sectors including engineering, textiles, pharmaceuticals, gems & jewellery, food processing, financial services, technology, education, and professional services are likely to benefit from improved market access and stronger commercial ties.

The accompanying Social Security Agreement further supports Indian professionals on temporary assignments in the UK by helping prevent double social security contributions, making international mobility more efficient for businesses and skilled workers.

As global trade continues to evolve, the implementation of CETA reinforces the commitment of both countries to deeper economic cooperation, sustainable growth, innovation, and stronger business partnerships. The agreement is expected to unlock fresh opportunities for companies seeking to expand internationally while contributing to increased trade, investment, employment, and long-term prosperity.

posts.title: Africa’s Green Minerals Drive a New Era of Industrial Partnerships, Clean Energy Investment, and Value-Added Manufacturing
posts.excerpt: Africa is rapidly emerging as one of the world’s most strategic destinations for critical minerals, which are essential for electric vehicles (EVs), renewable energy systems, battery storage, semiconductors, and advanced manufacturing. Minerals such as lithium, uranium, rare earth elements, cobalt, manganese, graphite, and copper are becoming increasingly important as governments and industries accelerate the global […]
posts.content:
Africa is rapidly emerging as one of the world’s most strategic destinations for critical minerals, which are essential for electric vehicles (EVs), renewable energy systems, battery storage, semiconductors, and advanced manufacturing. Minerals such as lithium, uranium, rare earth elements, cobalt, manganese, graphite, and copper are becoming increasingly important as governments and industries accelerate the global transition toward clean energy and digital technologies.

In a significant development, Namibia and China signed eight new cooperation agreements covering green minerals, infrastructure, energy, agriculture, science and technology, and economic partnership. The agreements are designed to move beyond traditional resource extraction by promoting local mineral processing, industrial value addition, technology transfer, workforce development, and long-term investment.

Unlike traditional mining agreements that focus primarily on exporting raw materials, the new partnership aims to develop downstream industries within Africa. This approach will encourage the establishment of mineral processing plants, battery material production, engineering services, manufacturing facilities, and supporting industrial infrastructure, enabling African economies to capture greater value from their natural resources while creating skilled employment opportunities.

The agreements also strengthen cooperation in infrastructure development, including transport networks, energy systems, and industrial facilities that are essential for supporting large-scale mining and manufacturing operations. Enhanced collaboration in science, technology, education, and workforce training is expected to improve local capabilities and accelerate industrial modernization across key sectors.

Namibia is particularly well positioned to become a strategic industrial hub. The country possesses significant reserves of uranium, lithium, and rare earth elements, while recent offshore oil discoveries and growing renewable energy projects further enhance its attractiveness as an investment destination. China already accounts for approximately one-quarter of Namibia’s exports, with uranium representing the majority of those shipments, and Chinese companies have invested billions of dollars in Namibia’s mining sector.

For businesses, the growing demand for critical minerals presents opportunities well beyond mining. Companies involved in engineering, heavy machinery, logistics, renewable energy, battery manufacturing, environmental services, construction, digital technologies, and industrial automation can all benefit from expanding projects across the continent.

posts.title: Asian Markets Surge on AI & Semiconductor Momentum

The positive market movement reflects sustained investor confidence in Asia’s rapidly expanding technology sector and its growing role in the global innovation ecosystem. The strong performance of technology-driven companies highlights increasing optimism around the future of AI, semiconductor development, […]
posts.content:
Asian equity markets advanced strongly as semiconductor and artificial intelligence-related companies led gains across the region. The positive market movement reflects sustained investor confidence in Asia’s rapidly expanding technology sector and its growing role in the global innovation ecosystem.

The strong performance of technology-driven companies highlights increasing optimism around the future of AI, semiconductor development, digital transformation, and advanced technologies. As demand for AI infrastructure and high-performance computing continues to grow, semiconductor companies remain at the centre of investor attention.

Asia has emerged as a critical hub for global technology manufacturing, innovation, and investment. Continued developments in AI and semiconductor industries are creating new opportunities for businesses, investors, and economies across the region.

The market momentum also demonstrates how technological advancement is increasingly influencing global investment trends. With innovation becoming a major driver of economic growth, Asia’s technology ecosystem continues to strengthen its position on the global stage.

For businesses and investors, the continued growth of AI and semiconductor industries presents significant opportunities for collaboration, investment, technological partnerships, and cross-border expansion.

posts.content:
Google has officially exceeded its US$1 billion investment commitment in Africa, marking a major milestone in the continent’s digital transformation journey. The investment is focused on expanding cloud infrastructure, strengthening AI research and innovation, improving internet connectivity, and equipping millions with digital skills needed for the future economy.

These initiatives are expected to accelerate entrepreneurship, attract global investment, support SMEs, and enhance Africa’s competitiveness in the global digital landscape. By improving access to advanced technologies and digital infrastructure, Google is helping create a stronger innovation ecosystem that can drive sustainable economic growth across the continent.

For businesses across Asia and Africa, this development opens new opportunities for digital trade, technology partnerships, cloud adoption, AI-driven solutions, and cross-border collaboration.

posts.title: India Emerges as Asia’s Top Equity Market Performer
posts.excerpt: India’s stock market has outperformed its major Asian peers, reflecting the country’s growing economic strength and increasing global investor confidence. posts.content:
India’s stock market has outperformed its major Asian peers, reflecting the country’s growing economic strength and increasing global investor confidence. Strong domestic inflows from retail and institutional investors, a resilient macroeconomic environment, and steady corporate earnings have helped Indian equities remain on a strong growth trajectory despite global market uncertainties.

The benchmark indices have continued to attract both domestic and foreign capital, supported by infrastructure development, digital transformation, manufacturing expansion, and government-led economic reforms. India’s diversified economy and stable financial system have further strengthened market sentiment, making it one of the most attractive investment destinations in Asia.

As global investors seek long-term growth opportunities, India’s capital markets are expected to play an increasingly significant role in the regional and global financial landscape, reinforcing the country’s position as a leading economic powerhouse.

posts.content:
Global financial institutions are increasingly expanding their operations across Asia, with South Korea standing out as a preferred destination for investment and regional headquarters. The country’s resilient economy, world-class infrastructure, transparent regulatory framework, and leadership in technology continue to attract international asset managers, banks, and investment firms.

This trend reinforces Asia’s rising importance in the global financial landscape while opening new opportunities for businesses, investors, and institutions seeking long-term growth. As capital flows into key Asian markets, South Korea is expected to play an even greater role in facilitating regional investment, innovation, and international collaboration.

For businesses across the Asian and African regions, this development highlights the growing potential for strategic partnerships, financial cooperation, and expanded market access in one of the world’s fastest-growing investment ecosystems.

posts.title: Sovereign Wealth Fuels Energy Boom Across Asia and Africa
posts.excerpt: Sovereign wealth funds are emerging as key drivers of the global energy transition, with nearly $29 trillion in capital expected to support renewable energy, power grids, storage, hydrogen, and other strategic infrastructure. As governments prioritize energy security, decarbonization, and long-term economic resilience, institutional investors are increasingly shifting portfolios toward sustainable assets. For Asia and Africa, […]
posts.content:
Sovereign wealth funds are emerging as key drivers of the global energy transition, with nearly $29 trillion in capital expected to support renewable energy, power grids, storage, hydrogen, and other strategic infrastructure. As governments prioritize energy security, decarbonization, and long-term economic resilience, institutional investors are increasingly shifting portfolios toward sustainable assets.

For Asia and Africa, this investment wave presents a unique opportunity to bridge infrastructure gaps, expand access to clean energy, attract foreign direct investment, and create millions of jobs. Countries that strengthen policy frameworks, improve investment climates, and develop bankable green projects will be well-positioned to benefit from this historic capital reallocation.

This trend highlights the growing importance of international collaboration between governments, financial institutions, and the private sector in building a cleaner, more resilient, and economically inclusive future.

posts.title: Asia’s AI Semiconductor Industry Gains Fresh Momentum as Global Demand Accelerates

Leading economies across the region are investing heavily in semiconductor fabrication, AI infrastructure, research, and next-generation chip technologies to meet rising international demand. With stronger public-private partnerships, supply chain diversification, and […]
posts.content:
The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence is driving unprecedented demand for advanced semiconductor chips, placing Asia at the center of the global technology ecosystem. Leading economies across the region are investing heavily in semiconductor fabrication, AI infrastructure, research, and next-generation chip technologies to meet rising international demand.

With stronger public-private partnerships, supply chain diversification, and continuous innovation, Asia is reinforcing its leadership in high-value manufacturing. The sector’s growth is expected to boost exports, attract foreign investment, generate skilled employment, and strengthen digital transformation across industries. For businesses, investors, and policymakers, the accelerating AI semiconductor market presents significant opportunities for cross-border collaboration and sustainable economic growth.

posts.title: India’s Exports Surge 18% in May
posts.excerpt: India’s export sector demonstrated remarkable resilience and growth in May, recording an impressive 18% year-on-year increase. The strong performance reflects growing international demand for Indian goods and services, improved manufacturing output, and the country’s expanding presence in global markets. Key sectors such as engineering goods, electronics, pharmaceuticals, chemicals, and textiles have continued to contribute significantly […]
posts.content:
India’s export sector demonstrated remarkable resilience and growth in May, recording an impressive 18% year-on-year increase. The strong performance reflects growing international demand for Indian goods and services, improved manufacturing output, and the country’s expanding presence in global markets. Key sectors such as engineering goods, electronics, pharmaceuticals, chemicals, and textiles have continued to contribute significantly to export growth, reinforcing India’s position as a major player in international trade.

The rise in exports is a positive indicator of economic momentum, showcasing the effectiveness of ongoing efforts to enhance competitiveness, strengthen supply chains, and diversify export destinations. As businesses increasingly explore opportunities across emerging and developed markets, India’s trade ecosystem continues to benefit from stronger global engagement and increased foreign demand.

However, despite the encouraging export performance, India’s trade deficit widened to $28.2 billion, highlighting the continued challenge of balancing imports and exports. A trade deficit occurs when the value of imports exceeds exports, and in India’s case, strong domestic demand, energy requirements, and imports of critical raw materials and industrial inputs continue to drive import growth.

While a higher trade deficit may present economic challenges, it also reflects a growing economy with rising consumption and industrial activity. Going forward, sustained export growth, increased value-added manufacturing, greater market diversification, and strategic trade partnerships will be crucial in narrowing the deficit and strengthening India’s overall trade balance.

The latest trade figures underscore both the opportunities and challenges facing India’s economy. As global trade dynamics continue to evolve, maintaining export competitiveness while managing import dependence will remain a key priority for policymakers and businesses alike.

posts.title: Iran conflict drives oil price surge, pressuring African fuel markets.
posts.excerpt: • Rising global oil prices linked to tensions involving Iran are sending economic shockwaves through fuel markets across Africa. • As most African nations rely heavily on imported refined petroleum, higher global prices are rapidly translating into increased fuel and transport costs. • Analysts warn that weaker currencies and higher energy import bills could accelerate inflation and place […]
posts.content:
• Rising global oil prices linked to tensions involving Iran are sending economic shockwaves through fuel markets across Africa.

• As most African nations rely heavily on imported refined petroleum, higher global prices are rapidly translating into increased fuel and transport costs.

• Analysts warn that weaker currencies and higher energy import bills could accelerate inflation and place additional strain on foreign reserves in vulnerable economies.

• While major oil exporters may benefit from higher revenues, households across the continent are likely to face rising living costs.

posts.content:
• Hong Kong offers a wide range of government funding programs aimed at strengthening business competitiveness and economic development.

• Incentive programs also focus on talent cultivation and startup incubation, encouraging entrepreneurship and skills development.

• These initiatives position Hong Kong as a supportive environment for SMEs, startups, and global businesses seeking growth opportunities in Asia.

posts.title: Dangote Cement posts record $730m profit, raises dividend, expands footprint.
posts.excerpt: • Dangote Cement Plc, Africa’s largest cement producer, reported a record net profit of US$730 million in 2025, more than doubling the previous year despite slightly lower sales volumes. • Revenue rose 20.3% to US$3.14 billion, supported by higher cement prices in Nigeria and strong cost-efficiency measures. • The company is expanding capacity across South Africa, Ethiopia, Senegal, Cameroon, and Zambia, while transitioning its logistics […]
posts.content:
• Dangote Cement Plc, Africa’s largest cement producer, reported a record net profit of US$730 million in 2025, more than doubling the previous year despite slightly lower sales volumes.

• Revenue rose 20.3% to US$3.14 billion, supported by higher cement prices in Nigeria and strong cost-efficiency measures.

• The company is expanding capacity across South Africa, Ethiopia, Senegal, Cameroon, and Zambia, while transitioning its logistics fleet to CNG for fuel savings and lower emissions.

• The board proposed a 50% increase in final dividend (approx. US$0.033 per share), signalling confidence amid Africa’s infrastructure and urbanisation momentum.

posts.title: India adopts a new GDP base year, reshaping macroeconomic measurement.
posts.excerpt: • On February 27, 2026, the National Statistics Office (NSO) under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation released a revised GDP series with base year 2022–23. • The update replaces outdated proxies with real-time digital and administrative datasets, reflecting India’s increasingly formalised and service-led economy. • The revision captures structural shifts over the past decade, including digitalisation, tax […]
posts.content:
• On February 27, 2026, the National Statistics Office (NSO) under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation released a revised GDP series with base year 2022–23.

• The update replaces outdated proxies with real-time digital and administrative datasets, reflecting India’s increasingly formalised and service-led economy.

• The revision captures structural shifts over the past decade, including digitalisation, tax reforms, financial inclusion, and expanded corporate reporting.

• For businesses and foreign investors, the recalibration enhances macroeconomic transparency, aligns India’s accounting practices with global standards, and supports more precise market forecasting.

posts.title: India revises its tax treaty with France, reshaping dividend and capital gains rules.
posts.excerpt: • India and France signed a Protocol amending their 1992 Double Taxation Avoidance Convention (DTAC), modernising the three-decade-old framework. • The revised treaty reduces dividend taxation for significant investors while expanding India’s rights to tax capital gains and cross-border share transfers. • The amendments align with India’s broader treaty renegotiation strategy emphasising source-based taxation, anti-avoidance safeguards, and greater legal clarity. […]
posts.content:
• India and France signed a Protocol amending their 1992 Double Taxation Avoidance Convention (DTAC), modernising the three-decade-old framework.

• The revised treaty reduces dividend taxation for significant investors while expanding India’s rights to tax capital gains and cross-border share transfers.

• The amendments align with India’s broader treaty renegotiation strategy emphasising source-based taxation, anti-avoidance safeguards, and greater legal clarity.

• French multinationals and portfolio investors may need to reassess dividend repatriation, exit strategies, and cross-border tax structuring under the updated regime.

posts.title: Several African economies are set to record the steepest food price increases in 2026.
posts.excerpt: • A new outlook from the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) projects sharp divergences in food inflation across 160 countries, with African nations dominating both the highest increases and notable declines. • Countries including Nigeria and Angola are expected to see some of the sharpest food price rises, driven largely by import dependence and currency pressures. • In contrast, Niger, Liberia, and Morocco are projected to […]
posts.content:
• A new outlook from the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) projects sharp divergences in food inflation across 160 countries, with African nations dominating both the highest increases and notable declines.

• Countries including Nigeria and Angola are expected to see some of the sharpest food price rises, driven largely by import dependence and currency pressures.

• In contrast, Niger, Liberia, and Morocco are projected to experience food price declines, supported by improved harvests and relative economic stability.

• The outlook underscores how domestic agricultural productivity, currency stability, and economic management are becoming decisive factors in shaping food inflation trends across the continent.

posts.title: Vietnam’s 2026 education reforms aim to boost FDI and workforce transformation.
posts.content:
• On December 10, 2025, Vietnam’s National Assembly approved major amendments to the Law on Education, Law on Vocational Education, and Law on Higher Education, effective January 1, 2026.
  • The reforms modernise regulatory frameworks across general, vocational, and higher education, aligning the sector with digitalisation and innovation-driven growth priorities.
  • By strengthening quality standards and institutional governance, the new framework enhances Vietnam’s attractiveness for foreign direct investment (FDI) in education and skills development.
  • The changes support long-term workforce competitiveness, reinforcing Vietnam’s strategy to integrate deeper into global value chains and high-tech industries

posts.title: South Africa’s debt burden is set to peak, signalling a fiscal turning point.
posts.content:
• South Africa’s government debt is projected to reach its highest level this year after nearly two decades of steady increases driven by weak growth and rising public expenditure.
  • Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana is expected to confirm that debt-to-GDP will stabilise and gradually decline.
  • A debt peak could ease interest payment pressures, creating fiscal space for targeted public spending ahead of municipal elections.
  • Strengthening economic indicators, currency stability, and lower bond yields are boosting investor confidence and reinforcing market optimism.

posts.content:
• Held in Addis Ababa and organised by the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa, the Forum urged long-term capital mobilisation to unlock Africa’s innovation potential and power inclusive growth.

• Leaders emphasised full implementation of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) to strengthen regional value chains, harmonise regulations, and enable cross-border enterprise expansion.

• Policymakers called for a shift toward ecosystem-based financing models, integrating infrastructure, industrialisation, digital markets, and green energy to generate sustainable employment.

• Heads of state, including Taye Atske Selassie and Salah Ahmed Jama, highlighted youth entrepreneurship, industrial policy, and digital transformation as central to Africa’s structural shift toward value-added growth.

• Intercompany loans and royalty payments generate recurring cross-border flows that directly affect taxable income and transfer pricing exposure.

• Withholding tax obligations on interest and royalties play a critical role in determining effective tax costs and compliance risk.

posts.title: The EU advances its Indo-Pacific trade strategy through India and Vietnam partnerships.
posts.excerpt: • The European Union concluded negotiations on a comprehensive India–EU Free Trade Agreement on January 27, 2026, marking a major milestone in EU–Asia trade relations. • In parallel, the EU upgraded its relationship with Vietnam to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, building on the existing EU–Vietnam Free Trade Agreement (EVFTA). • The two developments, announced days apart, reflect the EU’s sustained […]
posts.content:
• The European Union concluded negotiations on a comprehensive India–EU Free Trade Agreement on January 27, 2026, marking a major milestone in EU–Asia trade relations.

• In parallel, the EU upgraded its relationship with Vietnam to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, building on the existing EU–Vietnam Free Trade Agreement (EVFTA).

• The two developments, announced days apart, reflect the EU’s sustained commitment to the Indo-Pacific as a key region shaping the global economic and strategic order.• While the India–EU FTA has entered the legal scrubbing phase, full implementation will follow signature and ratification, highlighting differing timelines and strategic impacts compared with the already-operational EVFTA.

posts.title: Africa’s largest dam is turning Ethiopia into a regional power hub.
posts.excerpt: • The Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD) has lifted Ethiopia’s installed power capacity to 9.6 GW, doubling national electricity generation. • The project is catalysing industrial growth, agricultural irrigation, and large-scale electricity infrastructure, reshaping Ethiopia’s economic base. • Despite early disputes with Egypt and Sudan over Nile water flows, Ethiopia maintains the dam delivers shared regional benefits.• Financed largely through domestic mobilisation, […]
posts.content:
• The Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD) has lifted Ethiopia’s installed power capacity to 9.6 GW, doubling national electricity generation.

• The project is catalysing industrial growth, agricultural irrigation, and large-scale electricity infrastructure, reshaping Ethiopia’s economic base.

• Despite early disputes with Egypt and Sudan over Nile water flows, Ethiopia maintains the dam delivers shared regional benefits.• Financed largely through domestic mobilisation, GERD is positioning Ethiopia as an emerging regional electricity supplier, expanding cross-border power connectivity across the Horn of Africa.

• AGOA has been reauthorised only on a short-term basis, keeping the duty-free trade scheme in uncertainty.
  • The one-year extension fails to give businesses and investors long-term clarity or stability.
  • US Congress dropped plans to renew AGOA through the end of President Donald Trump’s term.
  • The scheme will now run only until 2027, reflecting the administration’s preference for limited extensions.

• Foreign ownership in Indonesia is allowed, but viability depends on activity-specific caps, scale thresholds, and licensing interpretation.
  • The Positive Investment List guides policy intent, but practical access is shaped by overlapping ownership, capital, and licensing rules.
  • Business activity classification determines ownership rights, local partner requirements, and long-term scalability.
  • Early feasibility analysis is critical, as structuring errors typically surface later during expansion, financing, or exit.

• Afreximbank has ended its credit rating relationship with Fitch Ratings after an internal review found the assessment misaligned with its mandate and legal framework.
  • The bank said Fitch’s ratings did not sufficiently reflect its Establishment Agreement, development role, and protections ratified by member states.
  • Afreximbank reaffirmed its financial resilience, citing strong shareholder support, legal safeguards, and a stable business profile.
  • The decision is likely to reopen debate on how global rating agencies assess African multilateral and development finance institutions.

• FSSAI issued draft amendments on January 20, 2026, to tighten outcome-based enforcement under the Food Safety and Standards licensing regulations, with a 60-day public consultation.
  • Annual return filing remains mandatory for all licensed food businesses, due by May 31 each year, with delays treated as non-compliance.
  • Penalties are proposed to be stricter, linked to license fees, with automatic license suspension for delays beyond 180 days.
  • Record-keeping and FIFO/FEFO stock rules apply mainly to manufacturers, while traders and retailers receive compliance relief.

• AfCFTA Secretary-General Wamkele Mene and Nigeria’s Finance Minister Wale Edun will headline Africa Business Convention 2026.
  • The event will be held on February 3–4, 2026, at the Lagos Continental Hotel in Nigeria.
  • Now in its fifth year, ABC has hosted over 8,700 delegates and 140 speakers, positioning it as a leading Africa-focused B2B platform.
  • ABC 2026 will focus on trade integration, investment, fiscal stability, and public–private action to support Africa’s growth agenda.

• India withdrew the Textile Machinery Safety QCO in January 2026, cancelling mandatory safety certification for imported textile machinery.
  • The rollback followed industry concerns over high compliance costs, supply disruptions, and lack of domestic alternatives.
  • Removal of the QCO allows unrestricted imports, reduces costs and delays, and supports textile sector modernization.
  • The decision provides short-term regulatory certainty, though a revised or phased framework may emerge later.

• Uganda’s long-delayed national oil refinery is moving closer to a $4 billion partnership with a UAE-backed investor, with a final investment decision targeted for 2026.
  • The planned 60,000 bpd refinery aims to cut Uganda’s $2 billion annual fuel import bill and support domestic value addition.
  • Ownership will be split between Alpha MBM Investments (60%) and Uganda National Oil Company (40%), reviving a project stalled for years.
  • The refinery is expected to serve regional markets in East and Central Africa, strengthening energy security and industrial growth.

• Budget 2026 is expected to focus on policy continuity, capital expenditure, digital transformation, and private investment.
  • Fintech, SaaS, AI, and Digital Public Infrastructure are being positioned as core economic and governance infrastructure.
  • India’s digital economy is projected to grow from about 12% of GDP to nearly 20% by 2030, driven by AI, cloud, and platforms.
  • Regulatory stability, skilling, R&D support, and export-oriented tech policies remain key priorities for investors and startups.

• Gujarat updated its Shops and Establishments rules in 2025 to modernize labor regulations and support business flexibility.
  • The applicability threshold increased to 20 employees, reducing compliance requirements for smaller firms.
  • Daily working hours were extended to 10, with a 12-hour spread-over limit and higher overtime allowances.
  • Women are now permitted to work night shifts, subject to consent, safety, and welfare conditions.

• SABA reported strong growth in 2025 with increased engagement across Scotland, London, and African markets.
  • Trade missions, inward delegations, and sector roundtables strengthened Scotland–Africa business ties.
  • Membership expanded across energy, skills, agriculture, maritime, and digital sectors, with rising African participation.
  • Africa remains a priority growth market, with expanded trade missions and advisory support planned for 2026.

posts.title: NRIs Continue to Miss DTAA Benefits Due to Documentation and Compliance Gaps
posts.content:
• India’s Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements are designed to prevent income from being taxed both in India and in an NRI’s country of residence, covering income such as interest, rent, capital gains, and professional fees.
  • Despite wide treaty coverage with nearly 100 countries, many NRIs overpay tax due to missing documents or incorrect application of DTAA provisions rather than ineligibility.
  • In the absence of valid DTAA documentation, banks and payers apply higher default TDS rates, often leading to excess tax payments and delayed refunds.
  • Experts note that accurate residency determination, proper treaty mapping, and timely filing of prescribed forms are essential to fully benefit from DTAA relief and improve cash flow.

posts.title: Africa’s Business Travel Sees Renewed Momentum
posts.content:
• Economic growth, regional integration, and infrastructure investment are driving a rebound in business travel across Africa.
  • New corporate travel hubs are emerging beyond South Africa, including Nairobi, Lagos, Kigali, Accra, and Addis Ababa, supported by expanding airline connectivity.
  • Increased activity in energy, finance, telecom, agribusiness, and technology is fueling more cross-border executive travel and deal-making.
  • While hybrid work has reduced routine trips, business travel is becoming more focused and strategic, reinforcing Africa’s long-term commercial integration.

posts.title: Africa’s Data Centre Boom Reshapes Energy and Digital Infrastructure Landscape
posts.content:
• Rapid digitalisation and the rise of AI are driving strong demand for data centres across Africa, with capacity in leading markets projected to grow sharply by 2030, extending beyond South Africa to countries such as Kenya, Nigeria, Egypt, and Morocco.
  • Power availability and reliability have emerged as the central constraint, as data centres are highly energy-intensive and outages carry significant operational risk.
  • Operators like Raxio Group are investing directly in power infrastructure and backup systems to ensure uptime, though this raises costs and complicates sustainability goals.
  • While renewable energy and solar PPAs offer long-term solutions, regulatory barriers persist in many markets, positioning East Africa—with its strong renewable base—as a potential future hub for greener data centre development.

posts.title: Saudi Arabia’s 2026 Budget Signals Opportunities and Pressures for Infrastructure Sector
posts.content:
• Saudi Arabia’s 2026 budget maintains strong support for infrastructure under Vision 2030, though cost-efficiency measures may affect project timelines and funding structures.
  • Spending discipline and global cost volatility are expected to intensify competition among contractors and pressure margins across long-term projects.
  • The budget outlines a multi-year pipeline in transport, urban development, and utilities, supported by growing use of PPPs and alternative financing models.
  • Firms with strong governance, regulatory compliance, and sustainable, technology-driven capabilities are likely to be best positioned as the Kingdom advances its transformation agenda.

posts.title: South Africa Increases Coal Exports to Israel Despite Diplomatic Tensions
posts.content:
• South African mining companies sharply increased thermal coal exports to Israel after Colombia imposed a ban, with shipments rising 87% year-on-year to 474,000 tonnes between August and November 2025.
    • Colombia, which previously supplied 41% of Israel’s coal imports, halted exports over Gaza-related concerns, creating a supply gap now largely filled by South Africa.
    • The trade expansion contrasts with South Africa’s strong diplomatic stance against Israel at the ICJ, highlighting a gap between foreign policy positions and commercial activity.
    • With Russia’s coal exports declining, South Africa is expected to supply about 55% of Israel’s coal imports in 2025, even as Israel plans to phase out coal by 2027.

posts.title: India–France Revise Tax Treaty to Clarify Dividend and Capital Gains Rules
posts.content:
• India and France have updated their 1994 double taxation treaty to modernize provisions, improve transparency, and rebalance taxing rights between the two countries.
  • The revised pact lowers dividend tax to 5% for French investors holding over 10% in Indian companies, while raising it to 15% for portfolio investors, encouraging long-term strategic stakes.
  • India gains broader rights to tax capital gains on all share sales by French investors, strengthening its authority over cross-border equity transactions.
  • Changes to technical services taxation and removal of the MFN clause are expected to reduce disputes and improve predictability for bilateral investment flows.

posts.title: Business Intelligence Seen as Key to Avoiding JV Disputes in Malaysia
posts.content:
• Malaysia continues to attract strong foreign investment, with RM51.5 billion in FDI in 2024 and RM150.8 billion in approved investments in the first nine months of 2025, underscoring sustained investor interest.
  • Experts note that most partnership disputes in Malaysian joint ventures arise from misunderstood authority and incentives, as real decision-making often sits with family owners rather than formal boards.
  • Business intelligence is increasingly used to map informal power structures, assess partner behaviour, and understand regulatory and relationship dynamics beyond official disclosures.
  • Early insight into hidden incentives and actual control is seen as critical to structuring realistic governance models and preventing disputes before major capital commitments are made.

posts.title: South Africa Advances $25 Billion National Grid Expansion
posts.content:
• Seven international consortia have been pre-qualified to bid for South Africa’s $25 billion (R440 billion) power grid upgrade, attracting global players from India, France, and China.
  • The project aims to modernise transmission infrastructure, reduce reliance on ageing coal plants, and support the integration of renewables, gas, and new technologies.
  • The first phase includes building 1,164 km of new transmission lines to connect about 3,000 MW of additional generation capacity.
  • Authorities see the expansion as critical for energy security, industrial growth, and economic recovery, with increased private-sector participation.

posts.title: Africa’s Business Heroes 2025 Grand Finale Celebrates Top Entrepreneurs in Kigali
posts.content:
• Entrepreneurs from Tanzania, Kenya, and South Africa emerged as winners at the 7th Africa’s Business Heroes Grand Finale held on December 13, 2025, in Kigali.
  • The grand prize of $300,000 went to Diana Orembe of Tanzania for NovFeed, which converts food waste into sustainable fish feed and organic fertilizer.
  • Kenya’s UzaPoint and South Africa’s NuvoteQ secured first and second runner-up positions, recognized for digital SME bookkeeping and clinical research solutions.
  • The Top 10 finalists were selected from over 32,000 applicants across Africa, sharing $1.5 million in grants under the Jack Ma Foundation initiative.

posts.title: Cambodia Clarifies Minimum Capital Rules for Foreign-Owned Companies
posts.content:
• Cambodia allows foreign-owned firms to register with a statutory minimum capital of KHR 4 million (about US$1,000), supporting an open investment environment.
  • In practice, banks and regulators expect higher paid-up capital to meet tax registration, licensing, and AML/KYC requirements.
  • Capital may be injected gradually, but companies must demonstrate adequate funds once operations commence, especially in regulated sectors.
  • Advisors recommend aligning declared capital with operational scale, as low capitalization can delay banking access, visas, and approvals.

posts.title: India’s AGILE-PRO-S Streamlines Six Key Business Registrations into One Form
posts.content:
• India’s AGILE-PRO-S (Form INC-35) under the SPICe+ system now enables companies to obtain GSTIN, ESIC, EPFO, professional tax (select states), bank account opening, and Shops & Establishments registration in a single filing.
  • The form is mandatory for all companies incorporated through SPICe+, covering Private Ltd, Public Ltd, OPCs, and Section 8 entities.
  • The unified process reduces compliance delays, supports faster market entry, and strengthens workforce-related registrations through automatic EPFO and ESIC allotment.
  • Updated under 2021 incorporation rules and expanded in March 2025, the system reinforces India’s shift toward a fully digital, investor-friendly business setup ecosystem.

posts.title: Africa Investment Forum 2025 Highlights Reduced Commitments but Stronger Project Readiness
posts.content:
• Investor commitments reached $15.3 billion across 39 projects, lower than 2024’s $29.5 billion, but with 95% of projects fully bankable.
  • Nearly 2,000 delegates from 80 countries attended, with energy and transport projects making up two-thirds of the pipeline.
  • Major financings included $275 million for Mauritania’s Zouerate–Nouadhibou railway and progress on Ethiopia’s $8.6–$12.5 billion Bishoftu Airport expansion.
  • AfDB launched a new project-tracking dashboard, strengthening implementation and ensuring investor commitments turn into real outcomes.

posts.title: Africa’s Fintech Landscape Strengthens as Ecosystem Models Drive Growth
posts.content:
• Africa’s fintech sector is accelerating as regulators, banks, telecoms and investors adopt ecosystem-based development across key markets.
  • Mobile money usage continues to expand, with over 330 million accounts pushing financial inclusion across the continent.
  • New policy frameworks in Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda and South Africa are creating clearer pathways for innovation and fintech scaling.
  • Strong activity from local and Africa-focused funds is sustaining momentum despite a global slowdown in venture investment.

posts.title: India Introduces New Telecom Cybersecurity Rules for 2025
posts.content:
• India’s amended TCS Rules introduce Telecom Identifier User Entities (TIUEs), covering banks, fintechs, e-commerce platforms, and messaging apps that use mobile-based authentication.
  • Messaging apps must enforce six-hour auto-logouts on web/desktop and adopt continuous SIM-based authentication to curb fraud.
  • OTT platforms such as WhatsApp, Telegram, Signal, and others now fall under mandatory data-sharing and cybersecurity compliance.
  • The reforms aim to strengthen cybercrime traceability, secure digital transactions, and increase accountability across telecom-linked services.

posts.title: AI Agents Positioned to Drive Africa’s Next Phase of Digital Transformation
posts.content:
• AI agents—systems that can perceive, reason, and act autonomously—are emerging as a major opportunity for accelerating digital modernization across Africa.
  • The global AI agents market, valued at US$5.4 billion in 2024, is projected to reach US$50–110 billion by 2030, reflecting annual growth above 45 percent.
  • Early enterprise adopters report higher productivity, reduced costs, and faster decision-making, with 75 percent viewing AI agents as a key source of competitive advantage.
  • With expanding digital adoption and persistent service gaps, Africa is seen as well-positioned to deploy AI agent solutions in business, public services, and inclusive innovation.

posts.title: Transform Africa Summit highlights push toward a Single Digital Market by 2030
posts.content:
• The 7th Transform Africa Summit in Conakry focused on advancing the continent’s goal of building a Single Digital Market through Smart Africa initiatives.
  • Theme centered on using AI to boost economic growth, sovereignty, and inclusive development, with key programs like SANIA, SADX, and Digital ID showcased.
  • New partnerships with Visa, YouthConnekt Africa, AFTLD, and others aim to expand digital payments, cybersecurity, skills development, and cross-border digital ID systems.
  • Smart Africa has grown to 42 member states, accelerating major projects that support Africa’s digital integration and global competitiveness.

posts.title: Vietnam’s manufacturing sector strengthens in 2025
posts.content:
• GDP grew 7.85% in the first three quarters of 2025, with industrial value-added up 9.92% and PMI reaching 54.5 — the strongest in over a year.
  • Manufacturing led growth with a 10.5% rise, boosted by surging export orders and renewed job creation across key sectors.
  • FDI reached US$31.52 billion in Jan–Oct, with manufacturing attracting over half; Singapore, China, and Hong Kong remained top investors.
  • New tax laws, industrial park upgrades, and green growth policies are helping Vietnam push toward its goal of becoming a top-three industrial economy in ASEAN by 2030.

posts.title: Norfund invests $75M in Mulilo Energy to boost renewables
posts.content:
• Norway’s development finance institution Norfund has invested $75 million in South Africa’s Mulilo Energy Holdings to support the country’s clean energy transition.
  • Mulilo operates 450 MW of solar and wind capacity, with another 765 MW under construction and a 30 GW pipeline that includes battery storage.
  • The investment comes through Norway’s Climate Investment Fund, reflecting strong international confidence in Africa’s renewable energy sector.
  • Mulilo’s expansion is guided by CEO Jan Oberholzer, former COO of Eskom, as the company accelerates its regional renewable growth.

posts.title: Eli Lilly’s Mounjaro becomes India’s top-selling drug
posts.content:
• Mounjaro (tirzepatide) overtook Augmentin as India’s highest-value drug in Oct 2025, generating ₹1 billion from just 85,000 units.
  • Sales reached ₹3.33 billion within seven months of launch, with usage far outpacing rival Wegovy.
  • Demand driven by rising obesity and diabetes, strong clinical results, and growing consumer awareness.
  • India’s GLP-1 market expanded about 27% YoY and is projected to grow over 34% annually through 2030.
  • Lilly deepening its India footprint with a US$1B investment and a new manufacturing hub in Hyderabad.
  • Regulatory focus increasing as obesity indication for tirzepatide awaits approval and semaglutide faces a 2026 patent expiry.

posts.title: Bloomberg confirms speakers and agenda for Africa Business Summit 2025
posts.content:
• Bloomberg will host the Africa Business Summit as a B20 South Africa sideline event on November 17–18, bringing together over 400 leaders from business, finance, and government.
  • The theme, “Unlocking Africa’s Investment Potential,” will focus on trade, innovation, AI, and the energy transition.
  • Speakers include Emrie Brown (RMB), Sim Tshabalala (Standard Bank), Abdul Samad Rabiu (BUA Group), and Emmanuel Lubanzadio (OpenAI).
  • The event will also feature Bloomberg’s New Voices cohort launch and the Africa Startups to Watch list recognizing high-impact entrepreneurs.
  • Discussions and panels will be broadcast live via Bloomberg Terminal, TV, and Bloomberg.com/live/emea.

posts.title: Delhi approves 24×7 business operations under new exemption policy
posts.content:
• The Delhi government issued “Delhi Exemption 2025,” allowing shops and commercial establishments (except liquor outlets) to operate 24×7.
  • The policy removes restrictions on working hours, weekly closures, and women’s night shifts—subject to strict safety and welfare conditions.
  • Establishments must provide secure transport, CCTV coverage, and safe workplaces, especially for night operations.
  • Approvals will be granted online by the Labour Department, with final clearance from the Lieutenant Governor.
  • The move aligns Delhi with states like Maharashtra and Karnataka, aiming to boost investments, modernize labor laws, and support round-the-clock urban business activity.

posts.title: India strengthens export frameworks for tech and electronics under STP & EHTP schemes
posts.content:
• STP (Software Technology Parks) and EHTP (Electronic Hardware Technology Parks) boost software and electronics exports through tax incentives and simplified regulations
  • Administered by the Software Technology Parks of India (STPI) under MeitY
  • STP supports IT, SaaS, and software exports; EHTP focuses on hardware, components, and embedded systems
  • Benefits include duty-free imports, 100% FDI, single-window clearance, and full repatriation of earnings
  • Firms must maintain positive Net Foreign Exchange within 5 years and file periodic reports to STPI
  • Schemes attract startups and foreign investors seeking low-cost, high-skill export bases in India’s tech ecosystem

posts.title: South Africa’s Business AI partners with Beyond Now to drive responsible enterprise AI
posts.content:
• Beyond Now’s Digital Marketplace to power Business AI, a South African startup under Mustek, focused on trusted and accessible AI for enterprises
  • Business AI introduces a secure framework and closed marketplace for companies to develop and share AI solutions
  • Backed by 16 major firms including Woolworths, Bidvest, and Stefanutti Stocks
  • Addresses low AI success rates through governed, vendor-agnostic, and responsible deployment models
  • Beyond Now’s marketplace enables co-development, monetization, and scalable AI innovation within an automated ecosystem

posts.title: Pepkor expands retail reach with R1.7 billion store acquisition
posts.content:
• South Africa’s largest clothing retailer acquires 469 stores worth R1.7 billion, strengthening its national footprint
  • Royal Caribbean’s Voyager of the Seas launches direct cruises from South Africa, boosting tourism and business travel
  • Fintech firm Platnova introduces Platnova Business, enabling cross-border transactions for African startups
  • Experts highlight the need for stronger investment in Africa’s creative industries through training and market access
  • Mali opens the $65 million Bougouni lithium project backed by UK and China, targeting leadership in lithium output by 2026

posts.title: Timor-Leste joins ASEAN, opening new investment frontiers
posts.content:
• Timor-Leste becomes ASEAN’s 11th member in October 2025, entering regional trade and policy frameworks
  • Gains full access to the ASEAN Economic Community and Free Trade Area with tariff-free regional trade benefits
  • TradeInvest Timor-Leste and SERVE streamline company registration and incentive approvals
  • Certified investors offered tax holidays up to 10 years, customs exemptions, and duty relief
  • Infrastructure upgrades, including Tibar Bay Port, enhance connectivity to ASEAN logistics routes
  • Key investment sectors include tourism, renewable energy, agribusiness, and public–private infrastructure projects

posts.title: India emerges as global hub for offshore accounting services
posts.content:
• Offshore accounting has evolved into a strategic necessity amid global talent shortages and digital finance growth
  • India leads as the top destination for CPA firms, offering skilled talent, English fluency, and time-zone advantages
  • U.S. accounting workforce down 17% since 2019, driving demand for offshore scalability
  • Indian teams provide 24-hour delivery cycles and on-demand capacity during tax and audit peaks
  • Strong data security and cloud-based tools ensure compliance and seamless collaboration

posts.title: Exxaro finalizes sale of FerroAlloys unit in employee-led deal
posts.content:
• Exxaro Resources sold its FerroAlloys subsidiary for R250 million ($13.8 million) to a consortium of employees, management, and EverSeed Energy
  • EverSeed Energy holds 60%, management 30%, and employees 10% through an ESOP
  • The transaction, completed on October 31, 2025, was financed via equity, debt, and vendor support
  • Exxaro will focus on coal, renewable energy, and energy transition metals including manganese
  • CEO Ben Magara said the deal strengthens employee alignment and supports the firm’s sustainable growth strategy

posts.title: Dr. Akintoye Akindele, CFA, DBA, FICA
posts.excerpt: Dr. Akintoye Akindele, CFA, DBA, FICAChairman, Founder & Managing Partner – Platform Capital | Board Advisor – AACCI Dr. Akintoye Akindele is a visionary investor, entrepreneur, and philanthropist with over two decades of experience in finance, private equity, and sustainable enterprise building across Africa and emerging markets. As the Founder, Chairman, and Managing Partner of […]
posts.content:
Dr. Akintoye Akindele, CFA, DBA, FICA
Chairman, Founder & Managing Partner – Platform Capital | Board Advisor – AACCI

Dr. Akintoye Akindele is a visionary investor, entrepreneur, and philanthropist with over two decades of experience in finance, private equity, and sustainable enterprise building across Africa and emerging markets. As the Founder, Chairman, and Managing Partner of Platform Capital, a Mauritius-headquartered investment and advisory firm with a portfolio exceeding USD 2 billion across five continents, Dr. Akindele has played a defining role in shaping the growth of numerous high-impact ventures across technology, energy, logistics, and education sectors.

He also serves as the Founder and CEO of Duport Midstream and Atlantic International Refineries & Petrochemicals Limited, leading the development of Nigeria’s first integrated energy park and pioneering modular refinery projects that redefine innovation in Africa’s energy infrastructure. Beyond business, Dr. Akindele’s passion for entrepreneurship, innovation, and education drives his commitment to empowering Africa’s next generation of leaders.

As Chairman of Diatom Impact and Co-Chairman of Liquidity Club, he continues to promote investment research, impact-driven enterprises, and global incubation networks that bridge Africa, Europe, and the Americas. His role as Professor at EM Normandie Business School (France) and Lecturer at the University of Lagos Business School underscores his dedication to mentorship and academic excellence.

Recognized globally, Dr. Akindele has received numerous honors including the Future Africa Award for Service to Young People, the African Leadership Magazine Award, and the State of Georgia Congressional Commendation (USA). His authored works, including Quitless – The Power of Persistence in Business and Life and A Love Affair with Failure, reflect his belief in resilience, innovation, and purpose-driven leadership. A Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA) and Doctor of Business Administration, Dr. Akindele combines deep financial acumen with a humanitarian vision — striving to position Africa as a global hub for trade, investment, and entrepreneurship.

posts.title: U.S. and Africa deepen cooperation on critical minerals
posts.content:
• Africa holds nearly 30% of global critical mineral reserves, vital for clean energy and AI industries
  • U.S.-Africa Business Center strengthens ties to diversify supply and reduce geopolitical risk
  • Critical Minerals Forum gathered over 300 leaders to advance sustainable partnerships
  • White Paper “Strategic Ground” outlines framework for cooperation and industrial growth
  • Focus on local value addition, infrastructure, and transforming Africa into a processing hub

posts.title: India’s luxury market set for $12.1B growth by 2025
posts.content:
• India’s luxury goods market projected to reach 12.1 billion dollars by 2025
  • Demand driven by young affluent buyers across major and emerging cities
  • Prime malls in Mumbai, Delhi, and Bengaluru report vacancy below 5 percent
  • Wedding and festive economy worth 75 billion dollars boosting couture demand
  • Italian brands gaining traction in bags, shoes, watches, and accessories
  • FDI-friendly policy with 100 percent single-brand retail ownership allowed
  • GST 2.0 rationalizes taxes; 18 percent standard rate for most luxury products
  • Localization and co-creation with Indian craft clusters seen as key strategy

posts.title: Small economies lead Africa’s 2025/26 investment rankings
posts.content:
• Seychelles, Mauritius, and Côte d’Ivoire take top positions in investor rankings
  • Governance and policy stability now outweigh market size for investors
  • South Africa slips due to structural constraints despite capital market strength
  • Nigeria drops on inflation and currency volatility
  • Morocco and Egypt gain from reforms and infrastructure programmes

posts.title: FirstRand acquires 20% stake in UAE fintech Optasia
posts.content:
• South Africa’s FirstRand Bank buys a 20 percent stake in Optasia
  • Transaction valued at about 70 million dollars
  • Optasia preparing for a Johannesburg Stock Exchange listing
  • Operates in 38 markets across Africa, the Middle East, and Asia
  • Partners include MTN, Vodacom, and Standard Bank
  • Expansion aimed at boosting digital lending and financial inclusion

posts.title: Vietnam and Finland upgrade to strategic partnership
posts.content:
• Ties elevated during President To Lam’s visit to Finland
  • Focus on trade, technology, and innovation cooperation
  • Finland becomes a gateway for Vietnamese goods into the EU
  • Vietnam positioned as Finland’s base in Southeast Asia
  • Expansion planned in AI, telecoms, clean energy, and startups
  • Major Finnish firms such as Nokia and KONE already present in Vietnam

posts.title: India and China will resume direct passenger flights by October 2025 after a five-year suspension.
posts.content:
• IndiGo will launch the first route from Kolkata to Guangzhou on October 26, 2025.
  • The move signals a gradual diplomatic thaw and renewed confidence between the two countries.
  • Direct flights will reduce travel costs and improve logistics for trade and investment.
  • Tourism and business travel are expected to rebound as mobility improves.
  • Stronger air links will support supply chains in electronics, pharma, renewables, and EPC sectors.
  • The reopening aligns with wider regional economic integration efforts under BRICS and RCEP.
  • It is seen as a confidence-building step that may lead to broader economic engagement.

posts.title: Global oil prices are sliding again as oversupply builds and demand cools
posts.content:
• Global crude is now approaching the $60 mark, its sharpest weekly fall since March due to weakening demand and rising supply
  • US output and inventories are climbing, fuelling expectations of a market glut by 2026
  • Broader geopolitical tensions and trade pressures are feeding investor caution
  • African oil exporters such as Nigeria, Angola and Libya face tighter budgets and reserve pressure as earnings shrink
  • Oil-importing African countries gain cost relief, but the benefit is limited by a stronger US dollar
  • Lower revenues are also increasing currency instability across several African markets

posts.title: Vietnam tourism surges with record arrivals and bold reforms
posts.content:
• Vietnam welcomed 13.9M foreign visitors Jan–Aug 2025, earning US$21.3B
  • E-visas, longer stays, golden visa plans, and broader checkpoints attract travelers
  • US$18B airport expansion by 2030 with Long Thanh under construction
  • Eco, wellness, and cultural tourism drive demand alongside luxury hotels
  • Industry eyes 35M visitors by 2030 and US$79.6B value by 2035

posts.title: Africa takes the lead at GABI 2025
posts.content:
• Africa steps up as driver of global trade and solutions
  • Leaders and investors push real business opportunities
  • Shift from raw exports to value creation across industries
  • AfCFTA aims to cut barriers and boost intra-African trade
  • Renewables, minerals, digital and creative sectors show strong growth potential

posts.title: Africa braces for trade upheaval with U.S. as key deal nears expiry
posts.excerpt: AGOA, the U.S. trade pact offering duty-free access for 32 African nations, is set to expire end of September 2025 South Africa holds steady on interest rates at 7 percent as central bank assesses recent policy moves Nigeria leads a continent-wide push to harmonize oil regulations through new forum AFRIPERF
posts.content:
AGOA, the U.S. trade pact offering duty-free access for 32 African nations, is set to expire end of September 2025

South Africa holds steady on interest rates at 7 percent as central bank assesses recent policy moves

Nigeria leads a continent-wide push to harmonize oil regulations through new forum AFRIPERF

posts.title: Markets in Asia fall amid growth concerns and U.S. rate uncertainty
posts.excerpt: Asian equities dip with MSCI Asia ex-Japan down 0.4 percent as investors fret about global slowdowns and Fed signals
posts.content: Asian equities dip with MSCI Asia ex-Japan down 0.4 percent as investors fret about global slowdowns and Fed signals

posts.title: Asia’s economies face mixed signals amid global headwinds:
posts.content:
• Asian manufacturing shrank in August amid rising U.S. tariffs, with Japan, South Korea, and Taiwan all posting contractions. China bucked the trend with a modest uptick in PMI, while India saw its fastest manufacturing growth in over 17 years.
  • The broader threat of deflation is emerging across Asia — excluding hotspots like Japan and Bangladesh — even as inflation remains high elsewhere globally.

posts.title: Vietnam has launched a direct overland fiber-optic link to Singapore, boosting digital connectivity across Southeast Asia
posts.content:
• The 3,900 km Vietnam–Singapore Terrestrial Network (VSTN) now links Da Nang to hubs in Thailand, Malaysia, and Singapore via land
  • Uses DWDM technology, offering 4 Tbps capacity (expandable to 12 Tbps) for high-speed data transfers
  • Reduces Vietnam’s reliance on unreliable undersea cables, improving resilience and control under VNPT’s ownership
  • A strategic move to support data centers, cloud services, fintech, and broader digital economy growth

posts.title: Singapore is ramping up its economic engagement in Africa:
posts.content:
• Trade in goods reached US \$12.4 bn in 2023, with over 100 Singaporean firms active.
  • Singapore Cooperation Enterprise now operates in 20 African countries, focusing on urban planning and infrastructure.
  • Africa-Singapore Business Forum 2025 will spotlight smart infrastructure, green finance, and digital innovation.

posts.title: African Economies Weathering Uncertainty with Modest Growth Gains
posts.content:
• Sub-Saharan Africa’s growth is projected to rise from 3.5% in 2025 to 4.3% by 2027, supported by sustained private consumption, investment, and cooling inflation.
  • Yet, this growth remains insufficient to seriously lower poverty levels, as millions still lack access to jobs, public services, and stable income.
  • Nigeria’s GDP recalibration and broader reforms are watched closely as the continent looks to translate economic metrics into tangible social progress.

posts.title: Saudi Launches 15 % VAT Refund Scheme for Tourists and GCC Visitors
posts.content:
• Saudi Arabia has launched a VAT refund program allowing tourists and GCC nationals to reclaim 15 % VAT on purchases over SAR 500.
  • Eligible goods must be unused, intended for personal export within 90 days, and purchased from participating stores.
  • Refund claims are validated at airport kiosks in Riyadh, Jeddah, and Dammam before departure.
  • Refunds are issued via cash (up to SAR 5,000/day) or card—though only card payments are accepted at select terminals.
  • The initiative supports the Kingdom’s Vision 2030 by enhancing its attractiveness as a retail and tourism destination.

posts.title: UAE to roll out mandatory e-invoicing for VAT-registered businesses by 2026
posts.content:
• The UAE will implement mandatory e-invoicing for all VAT-registered businesses starting in late 2024, with full rollout by Q2 2026
  • Invoices must be submitted digitally in XML or JSON format via accredited service providers; paper or scanned invoices will not be accepted
  • The system uses a five-corner model through the Peppol network, involving the issuer, receiver, both service providers, and the FTA platform
  • Each member of a VAT group must have a separate endpoint for invoice submission to ensure traceability
  • Businesses should prepare by auditing systems, selecting ASPs, and training staff to meet compliance requirements

posts.title: Japan boosts Africa focus with investments, AI schools, and youth jobs push
posts.content:
• Japan strengthens its Africa strategy through investments in climate resilience, infrastructure, and human development
  • Over \$2.9 billion in co-financed projects with the African Development Bank are underway, including training nearly 300,000 African officials
  • The upcoming TICAD9 summit will spotlight youth employment, digital transformation, and regional trade integration
  • Japan plans to expand partnerships through multilateral forums with nations like Indonesia, Brazil, and Turkey
  • Meanwhile, Nigeria receives \$21 billion in remittances, while women-led caterpillar businesses rise in Burkina Faso

posts.title: South Africa Secures \$398 Million Loan for Road Infrastructure Upgrade
posts.excerpt: South Africa is set to receive a R7 billion loan from the New Development Bank (NDB) to enhance its road infrastructure.The loan will focus on upgrading key transportation routes, reducing congestion, and improving safety.The NDB is becoming a major alternative to Western financiers for infrastructure projects in the Global South.The project aims to meet rising […]
posts.content:
South Africa is set to receive a R7 billion loan from the New Development Bank (NDB) to enhance its road infrastructure.
The loan will focus on upgrading key transportation routes, reducing congestion, and improving safety.
The NDB is becoming a major alternative to Western financiers for infrastructure projects in the Global South.
The project aims to meet rising transport demands after years of underinvestment and will support economic recovery.
SANRAL plans to upgrade four major freeways and other related infrastructure, with job creation and sustainability as key priorities.

posts.title: India and UK Sign Historic Free Trade Agreement
posts.excerpt: India and the UK signed a major Free Trade Agreement, enhancing bilateral economic ties.The deal offers zero or reduced tariffs on 99% of Indian exports and duty-free access for 64% of UK exports to India.Key sectors like textiles, pharmaceuticals, and auto parts in India are expected to see a 20-40% export boost.The agreement fosters greater […]
posts.content:
India and the UK signed a major Free Trade Agreement, enhancing bilateral economic ties.
The deal offers zero or reduced tariffs on 99% of Indian exports and duty-free access for 64% of UK exports to India.
Key sectors like textiles, pharmaceuticals, and auto parts in India are expected to see a 20-40% export boost.
The agreement fosters greater market access for UK luxury goods, digital services, and clean energy investments.
The trade deal is set to create thousands of jobs and contribute an additional £4.8 billion annually to the UK’s GDP.

posts.title: South Africa Secures \$398 Million Loan for Road Infrastructure Upgrade
posts.excerpt: South Africa is set to receive a R7 billion loan from the New Development Bank (NDB) to enhance its road infrastructure.The loan will focus on upgrading key transportation routes, reducing congestion, and improving safety.The NDB is becoming a major alternative to Western financiers for infrastructure projects in the Global South.The project aims to meet rising […]
