• Over 720,000 NSFAS beneficiaries affected by student debt, with more than 120,000 unable to register due to unpaid fees.
  • Universities withholding certificates from students with outstanding debt, impacting job opportunities.
  • Four suspects arrested for setting fire to over 50 Putco buses in Mpumalanga, facing property damage charges.
  • Attack involved armed individuals targeting employees and multiple depots.
  • Mabopane residents demand urgent action from Tshwane Municipality over ongoing sewage spillages.
  • Health risks include tuberculosis concerns due to unsanitary conditions.
  • Sewage issues damaging roads and causing toilet overflows, disrupting daily life.

posts.title: US Freezes Aid to South Africa Over Land Ownership Dispute
posts.content:
• President Trump froze US aid to South Africa, citing concerns over a law allowing land seizure from white farmers.
  • Land ownership remains a contentious issue in South Africa, with most farmland still owned by white people post-apartheid.
  • The South African government denies claims of seizing land under the expropriation act.
  • The US aims to promote resettlement of Afrikaner refugees amid allegations of race-based discrimination.
  • Elon Musk criticizes South Africa’s ownership laws for affecting his Starlink satellite internet service licensing.

posts.title: Vietnam and Czechia Elevate Ties to Strategic Partnership
posts.content:
• Vietnam and Czechia upgraded bilateral relations to a Strategic Partnership during Prime Minister Pham Minh Chinh’s visit to Czechia on January 20, 2025.
  • The partnership aims to deepen cooperation in defense, security, trade, investment, education, science and technology, environment, healthcare, and tourism.
  • Trade between Vietnam and Czechia has grown significantly under the EU-Vietnam Free Trade Agreement (EVFTA).
  • Prime Minister Pham urged increased collaboration in emerging industries such as semiconductor production, AI, and biotechnology.
  • Czech automaker Škoda plans to start vehicle production in Vietnam, viewing it as a gateway to ASEAN countries.
  • Czech investment in Vietnam includes a substantial stake in the Mong Duong 2 coal-fired power plant.
  • Defense and security cooperation will focus on exchanges, information sharing, and combating transnational crimes.
  • Economic cooperation will be strengthened through the Vietnam-Czechia Intergovernmental Committee, focusing on renewable energy, pharmaceuticals, and infrastructure.
  • The partnership also emphasizes collaboration in education, science, technology, environmental practices, and global and regional issues at international forums.

posts.title: South Africa Introduces AI-Powered Visa Reforms for India and China
posts.content:
• President Ramaphosa announced reforms to South Africa’s visa regime, aiming to boost tourism and business from India and China.
  • An Electronic Travel Authorisation system will be launched to streamline visa applications using AI, reducing corruption and processing times.
  • Indian companies and diplomats in South Africa laud the reforms, expecting easier visa processes and increased business opportunities.
  • CEO Ashish Sharma anticipates increased tourist traffic and potential for direct flights between India and South Africa.
  • Gourish Chakravorthy highlights the benefits of digital visa reforms in enhancing tourism and economic contributions to South Africa.

posts.title: Philippines Tightens Work Permit Rules for Foreign Nationals
posts.content:
• Under the new guidelines, employers can file AEP applications for foreign nationals before they arrive in the Philippines, with issuance upon entry, reducing delays.
  • More stringent job advertisement requirements now include newspaper, PhilJobNet, and PESO/JPO postings, detailing comprehensive job and applicant information.
  • Longer processing times are expected due to extended AEP application periods and stricter compliance checks.
  • Mandatory Certificate of Exemption now required for previously exempted foreign workers, formalizing regulatory oversight.
  • Higher costs anticipated from increased job advertisement obligations and administrative steps for hiring foreign talent.

posts.title: GABI Report Pushes Inclusive Financing for Africa’s Economic Growth
posts.content:
• GABI’s 2024 report calls for inclusive financing models to unlock Africa’s economic potential through concessional financing and private sector investment.
  • African institutions are urged to lead global risk perceptions and innovate financial solutions for sustainable investments.
  • “Unstoppable Africa” 2024, a premier event during the UN General Assembly, attracted global leaders to discuss transformative strategies for Africa’s economic future.
  • Key initiatives include Mission 300 for clean energy access and Itana, Africa’s first Digital Economic Zone, fostering digital skills and economic growth.
  • Creative industries and sports are highlighted as drivers of economic growth and cultural diplomacy in Africa’s development agenda.

posts.title: Egypt and UAE Strengthen Ties with $35 Billion Ras El-Hekma Project
posts.content:
• Egypt-UAE discussions focused on the Ras El-Hekma project, a strategic development zone on Egypt’s northwest coast.
  • Egyptian PM Madbouly met UAE ministers to strengthen bilateral ties and review joint projects.
  • Ras El-Hekma project, backed by UAE’s ADQ with a $35 billion investment, aims to develop a smart, sustainable city with tourism hubs, infrastructure, and more.
  • Discussions included collaborations in petroleum, gas, data centers, and airport management sectors.
  • Focus on renewable energy projects like Benban solar hub aligns with Egypt’s economic goals for clean energy and infrastructure development.

posts.title: Nigeria Begins Tolling on Abuja-Akwanga-Lafia-Makurdi Expressway
posts.content:
• The Federal Government will begin tolling operations on Abuja-Akwanga-Lafia-Makurdi Expressway this Tuesday.
  • Minister of Works, Engr. David Umahi, will officiate the ceremony at Garaku Toll Station, KM 32 on the Keffi-Akwanga section.
  • The expressway features four toll stations, sparking concerns among road users and transporters about potential fare impacts.
  • Further details to follow as reported by LEADERSHIP.

posts.title: Kuwait Introduces Stricter Workforce Regulations
posts.content:
• Kuwait has implemented new workforce regulations focusing on stricter housing norms and mandatory fingerprint attendance for government projects.
  • The Public Authority of Manpower (PAM) introduced housing regulations ensuring no more than four individuals per room and housing allowances if standards aren’t met.
  • Mandatory biometric attendance systems are now required for workers on government projects to enhance accountability and efficiency.
  • Kuwait has adjusted policies to facilitate labor mobility, allowing expatriates to transfer permits upon project completion under specific conditions.
  • Despite efforts to nationalize the workforce, expatriates constitute a significant majority in Kuwait’s private sector, highlighting ongoing demographic challenges.

posts.title: Trump Announces Funding Cut to South Africa Over Land Reform Concerns
posts.content:
• Donald Trump announced cutting funding to South Africa due to alleged human rights violations, specifically citing land confiscation and mistreatment of certain groups.
  • Trump criticized South Africa on Truth Social, accusing the Radical Left Media of ignoring the situation.
  • Allegations include claims of divisive land issues and efforts to address apartheid-era inequalities between white and black citizens.
  • South African President Cyril Ramaphosa signed a bill allowing for “nil compensation” in certain public interest expropriations, sparking controversy.
  • Land ownership remains a contentious issue in South Africa, with the majority of farmland still owned by white people post-apartheid.

posts.title: India and Oman Advance CEPA Talks to Boost Trade and Investment
posts.content:
• Indian Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal concluded a successful visit to Muscat, advancing Oman-India CEPA negotiations.
  • Bilateral trade between Oman and India in 2023-24 valued at US$8.94 billion, with discussions focusing on reducing tariffs.
  • CEPA negotiations, initiated in November 2023, aim to enhance trade in goods, services, and investments.
  • Goyal co-chaired the 11th India-Oman Joint Commission Meeting, emphasizing cooperation in trade, technology, and renewable energy.
  • A protocol to amend the India-Oman DTAA was signed to streamline tax procedures and encourage economic collaboration.
  • Goyal engaged with key Omani leaders and business forums to strengthen economic ties and explore investment opportunities.
  • Discussions also highlighted cultural engagements, India’s economic growth, and people-to-people connections with Oman.

posts.title: Vietnam Expands Bonded Warehouse Network for Global Trade
posts.content:
• Establishing a bonded warehouse in Vietnam supports international trade logistics, providing secure storage before customs clearance.
  • Regulatory framework includes Customs Law and specific decrees guiding warehouse establishment and operation.
  • Key steps involve document submission to Customs, including business registration and layout plans.
  • Customs review ensures compliance with location, security, and operational standards.
  • Benefits include deferred import duties, streamlined export processes, and enhanced operational efficiency.
  • Locations across Vietnam include major cities and industrial parks, optimizing logistical advantages for businesses.

posts.title: Africa Advances in Fight Against Neglected Tropical Diseases
posts.content:
• River-dwelling blackflies transmit microparasites causing river blindness, a neglected tropical disease affecting millions.
  • Neglected tropical diseases impact over 600 million people in Africa, particularly in remote areas with limited healthcare access.
  • Modern medicine has made most of these diseases preventable or treatable, with 21 African countries recognized for progress since 2013.
  • Niger becomes the first African country to eliminate river blindness, marking a significant milestone.
  • Future progress depends on well-funded national programs and strong leadership in Africa.
  • Ethiopia increases domestic commitments to disease control, aiming for sustainable health improvements and economic growth.
  • Integration of care into primary healthcare systems in Ethiopia enhances early detection and treatment accessibility.
  • Investments in disease control are cost-effective and yield long-term economic benefits by enabling greater workforce participation.
  • The Reaching the Last Mile Fund supports elimination efforts across Africa and Yemen through partnerships and funding.
  • Country-led initiatives like Ethiopia’s align with broader development goals, ensuring sustainable progress against these diseases.

posts.title: Odisha Emerges as a Key Investment Destination
posts.content:
• Odisha boasts the Paradip port, linking it to key trade hubs in South and Southeast Asia.
  • The state attracts investments in chemicals, petrochemicals, textiles, mining, renewable energy, IT/ITeS, tourism, and food processing.
  • GO SWIFT portal simplifies approvals, while IPR 2022 offers incentives like subsidies, exemptions, and SGST reimbursements.
  • Rich in minerals like iron ore, coal, and bauxite, Odisha supports robust industrial growth in metals and minerals.
  • Industrial parks, food processing zones, and IT hubs enhance Odisha’s appeal for diverse investments.

posts.title: Namibia Advances Green Hydrogen and Renewable Energy Projects
posts.content:
• Namibia has applied for US$150 million from the Climate Investment Fund to develop a green hydrogen production sector.
  • Projects are expected to start production in 2025.
  • Namibia’s Green Hydrogen Commissioner James Mnyupe leads efforts through the Namibia Green Hydrogen Council.
  • Hylron plans to launch a green iron production facility near Arandis, Erongo region, by February.
  • Hylron’s Oshivela plant will use a 25MW solar facility for green iron production.
  • Namibia aims to construct its first ammonia bunkering facility this year for ship refueling.
  • Hydrogène de France (HDF) Energy Namibia plans a renewable energy plant in Erongo for baseload power.
  • HDF aims to generate 142 GWh of green electricity annually for Swakopmund municipality.

posts.title: Kala Ghoda Arts Festival: Reviving Mumbai’s Cultural Legacy
posts.content:
• Once home to the Sassoon family, Kala Ghoda was a hub of culture, education, and business in 19th and 20th century Mumbai.
  • The area boasts architectural gems like the David Sassoon Library, Army & Navy Building, and Prince of Wales Museum.
  • Despite a late 20th-century decline, cultural landmarks like Rhythm House and Jehangir Art Gallery kept the area vibrant.
  • The Kala Ghoda Arts Festival, launched 26 years ago, is Asia’s largest street arts festival celebrating architecture, arts, and heritage.
  • The festival offers over 400 programs, including music, dance, theatre, literature, and food events across 25 venues.
  • Funds from the festival support the restoration of heritage sites, with backing from the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation.
  • Initially held on the streets, it now spans multiple venues and attracts a diverse audience, including students.
  • Despite challenges like security concerns and funding issues, the festival remains a key event in Mumbai’s cultural scene.
  • Highlights include a new anthem, diverse performances, and sessions on dance, mythology, poetry, and culinary arts.
  • The festival emphasizes Mumbai’s rich heritage and cultural diversity through 15 thematic verticals.

posts.title: Africa: Balancing AI and Human Agency in Education
posts.content:
• nternational Day of Education 2025 theme emphasizes “AI and education: Preserving human agency in a world of automation.”
  • AI transforms education with personalized learning and automated grading, improving efficiency and teacher focus on student needs.
  • Raises concerns about maintaining human control, stressing the need for balanced integration of AI in education.
  • In Africa, AI offers solutions to educational challenges while emphasizing human-centric values and local accountability.
  • Strengthening education data systems is vital for effective AI implementation and context-specific outcomes.
  • Highlights the importance of teaching critical thinking and responsible AI use to complement human skills like empathy and creativity.
  • Educator training in AI integration is crucial for fostering human-centered teaching practices.
  • The future of education lies in harmoniously blending AI and human capabilities to address evolving global challenges.

posts.title: Union App Launches to Empower Uganda’s Boda Boda Riders
posts.content:
• Launch event held at Kampala Serena Hotel under the theme “Empowering Boda Boda Riders for Growth.”
  • New app connects riders with travelers, boosting industry efficiency.
  • Union Chairperson Frank Mawenje attributes the app idea to patriotism training at Kaweweta.
  • Initiatives focus on protecting riders from extortion and unfair pricing practices.
  • United Boda Boda Riders Cooperative Union established to provide financial support.
  • Legal counsel aims to improve public perception of riders and offer legal assistance.
  • The union seeks to unify operators nationwide, with attendees from all regions at the event.

posts.title: FSSAI Mandates Nutritional Transparency on Food Labels by July 2024
posts.content:
• FSSAI sets July 1 as the annual enforcement date for amendments to labeling regulations.
  • Nutritional details like total sugar, salt, and saturated fat must be displayed on food labels starting July 6, 2024.
  • Regulations require clear labeling of ingredients, nutritional values, allergens, and front-of-pack information.
  • Fixed enforcement date ensures predictable compliance timelines for businesses and consumers.
  • Benefits include enhanced transparency, operational efficiency, and reduced packaging changes.

posts.title: Saudi Arabia Revises Labor Laws to Boost Worker Protections and Job Security
posts.content:
• Saudi Arabia’s Labor Law amendments take effect in February 2025, enhancing worker protections and employer obligations.
  • Aligns with Vision 2030 goals to promote job security and human capital development.
  • Employer responsibilities expanded to include clear regulations on grievance procedures, leave entitlements, and contract terms.
  • Introduces new frameworks for employment contracts, including maritime employment.
  • Employers urged to update contracts, policies, and training programs to comply with the revised labor laws.

posts.title: Russia’s Strategic Role in Central African Republic Amid Controversy
posts.content:
• Rebels in Syria opposed Assad, while Kremlin-backed mercenaries supported President Touadéra in CAR.
  • Touadéra relies on Wagner Group for protection, according to a rebel alliance spokesperson.
  • Russia strengthens African ties, including security cooperation, as highlighted by Putin’s meeting with Touadéra in Moscow.
  • Russian military presence in Africa counters Western influence, supporting regimes and filling gaps left by Western withdrawals.
  • Wagner-linked companies control mining concessions in CAR amidst allegations of human rights abuses.
  • Russia’s involvement in CAR and Mali faces criticism over atrocities reportedly committed by Wagner forces.

posts.title: Ghana Explores BRICS+ Partnership to Boost Global Influence
posts.content:
• Ghana considers joining BRICS+ as a ‘partner state’ to enhance its geopolitical and economic standing.
  • Partnership would signify Ghana’s deeper engagement in global multilateral institutions.
  • The New Development Bank under BRICS offers significant financial backing for development initiatives.
  • BRICS+ framework prioritizes non-interference and cooperation, aligning with Ghana’s growth and diplomatic goals.

posts.title: Saudi Arabia Introduces Labor Law Amendments to Strengthen Worker Protections
posts.content:
• Amendments effective February 2025 focus on enhancing worker protections and expanding employer obligations.
  • Changes align with Vision 2030 goals, emphasizing job security, human capital development, and better work environments.
  • Employer responsibilities now include improved grievance procedures, clear leave entitlements, and detailed contract terms.
  • New regulations address resignation processes, probation periods, and employment conditions.
  • Reforms aim to boost employee rights and workplace conditions across Saudi Arabia.

posts.title: AU Targets 45% Agri-Food Output Growth by 2035
posts.content:
• AU adopts a 10-year CAADP Strategy and Action Plan for resilient agri-food systems.
  • Goals include reducing post-harvest losses by 50% and tripling intra-African agri-food trade by 2035.
  • Ugandan President emphasizes value addition to reduce reliance on imports.
  • Calls made to eliminate non-tariff barriers disrupting agriculture across Africa.
  • AU Commission raises concerns over the slow progress of the CAADP Programme since 2014.
  • Collective action stressed to achieve food sovereignty and prosperity under Agenda 2063.

posts.title: India-Singapore Partnership Strengthens with President’s Visit
posts.content:
• India and Singapore maintain strong ties under the Strategic Partnership, with Singapore as India’s largest trade partner in ASEAN.
  • Singapore is India’s top source of FDI, supporting urban planning and infrastructure.
  • Singaporean President Tharman Shanmugaratnam’s visit to India is the first by a Singaporean president in a decade.
  • Trade under the Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Agreement reached $35.61 billion in FY 2024.
  • Economic cooperation spans digital connectivity, fintech, green economy, and healthcare.

posts.title: Africa’s Fuel Prices Reflect Oil Wealth and Economic Policies
posts.content:
• Libya: Fuel costs $0.030 per litre, driven by abundant oil reserves crucial to its economy.
  • Angola: Prices at $0.328 per litre, supported by substantial oil production and global market presence.
  • Egypt: Fuel priced at $0.336 per litre, with government subsidies maintaining affordability amid sector investments.
  • Algeria: Costs $0.339 per litre, leveraging vast oil and gas resources and government subsidies for economic stability.
  • Sudan: Fuel priced at $0.700 per litre, benefiting from domestic production despite economic challenges.
  • Nigeria: Prices at $0.769 per litre, influenced by global oil fluctuations and local economic factors despite being a major oil exporter.
  • Tunisia: Fuel costs $0.794 per litre, with limited domestic production but regional market access and subsidies.
  • Ethiopia: Priced at $0.805 per litre, imports fuel with government efforts stabilizing prices for consumers.
  • Liberia: Fuel at $0.829 per litre, reliant on imports and supported by government policies and trade agreements.
  • Gabon: Costs $0.944 per litre, benefited by significant oil reserves despite higher prices compared to larger oil producers.

posts.title: Pacific Defense Strategies Shift Amid Rising Geopolitical Tensions
posts.content:
• The U.S. and Pacific allies reassess defense priorities in response to threats from China, Russia, and North Korea.
  • Japan’s remilitarization includes new aircraft carriers, mirroring WWII-era maritime strategies.
  • The U.S. expands its Pacific presence with bases in the Philippines and technology partnerships with Australia.
  • Obama’s “Pivot to Asia” strategy underscored U.S. long-term interests in the Indo-Pacific.
  • China’s naval expansion, featuring AI-powered vessels and hypersonic capabilities, challenges U.S. dominance.
  • Okinawa’s strategic role persists despite local opposition, shaping U.S.-Japan defense strategies.
  • Guam faces logistical hurdles with housing shortages and unstable power supply amid military buildup.
  • Tinian redevelopment aims to strengthen U.S. Pacific air defense while reducing disruption in Guam and Okinawa.

posts.title: Challenges Threaten Growth of Asia’s Middle Class
posts.content:
• Asia’s middle class growth is slowing, raising concerns for the “Asian Dream”.
  • Despite significant contributions to global GDP, economic momentum in Asia is stagnating.
  • Indonesia’s middle class decline highlights broader economic challenges post-pandemic.
  • China’s real estate collapse is affecting household wealth and spending habits.
  • A strong middle class is vital for driving political and economic development.
  • Optimism remains high among many Asians despite economic slowdowns.
  • Effective government policies are essential to sustain middle-class growth amid shifts.
  • Emerging-market middle classes are expected to double by 2034, led by Asia.
  • Maintaining middle-class status requires sustainable economic policies and investments

posts.title: Kenya Set to Release Grade 6 KPSEA Exam Results
posts.content:
• Nairobi: Grade 6 results for KPSEA exams to be announced soon.
  • Education CS advises parents and students to check school portals for results.
  • Ministry of Education disburses Sh48.4 billion to public schools.
  • Funds allocated include Sh4.13 billion for Free Primary Education, Sh15.33 billion for Free Day Junior School Education, and Sh28.92 billion for Free Day Secondary School Education.

posts.title: Ghana Offers Visa-Free Travel for All African Passport Holders
posts.content:
• All African passport holders can now visit Ghana visa-free, effective from the start of this year.
  • Ghana becomes the fifth African country to provide visa-free travel to all other African nations.
  • Visa-free travel within Africa promotes pan-African values and strengthens economic cooperation.
  • Ghana aims to boost tourism and economic ties with other African countries through this initiative.
  • Outgoing President Akufo-Addo emphasized this as a step towards aligning with the African Continental Free Trade Area.

posts.title: Bahrain Introduces Regulations for Domestic Minimum Top-Up Tax
posts.content:
• Bahrain has published supplementary regulations for its Domestic Minimum Top-Up Tax (DMTT).
  • These regulations complement the primary DMTT law introduced in September 2024.
  • Multinational enterprises (MNEs) operating in Bahrain must assess their DMTT impact and register by January 30, 2025.
  • The regulations align with OECD’s Global Anti-Base Erosion (GloBE) Model Rules, adapted to Bahrain’s tax framework.
  • Registration requires MNEs to appoint a Filing Constituent Entity and make quarterly advance payments starting in 2025.
  • Immediate action is crucial for businesses to avoid penalties and ensure smooth transition into the new tax regime.

posts.title: Uganda: Electricity Tariffs Go Down By 5.2% – ERA Announces
posts.content:
• ERA announces a 5.2% reduction in electricity tariffs for Q1 2025.
  • Domestic consumer tariff decreases from shs 803.0 to shs 606.2 per unit.
  • Commercial consumers’ tariff set at shs 575.2 per unit.
  • Medium manufacturers to pay shs 417.8 per unit; large industries shs 351.5 per unit.
  • Public amenities tariff fixed at shs 360.0 per unit; extra-large industries at shs 299.1 per unit.
  • Reduction expected to save shs 155 billion in electricity delivery costs.
  • Lower tariffs attributed to anticipated demand growth and upcoming energy projects.
  • Future tariff adjustments to consider inflation, exchange rates, and fuel prices.
  • Street lighting included under the new public amenities category.
  • Declining block tariff structure to continue for large industrial consumers.

posts.title: Global Factory Activity Slumps Amid Trade Risks
posts.content:
• Factory activity in Europe and Asia ended 2024 on a weak note due to trade risks and economic uncertainties.
  • Euro zone manufacturing continued to decline, with Germany, France, and Italy in an industrial recession.
  • Asian manufacturing showed mixed results; China and South Korea slowed, while Taiwan and Southeast Asia improved.
  • President-elect Trump’s tariff pledges increased global trade tensions, particularly with Mexico, Canada, and China.
  • China’s manufacturing PMI fell to 50.5 in December, indicating modest growth despite policy support.

posts.title: Thailand Launches Employee Welfare Fund for Financial Security
posts.content:
• Thailand introduces Employee Welfare Fund from October 1, 2025, under Labor Protection Act B.E. 2541 (1998).
  • Employers and employees contribute 0.25% of wages from 2025 to 2030, increasing to 0.5% thereafter.
  • Contributions due by the 15th of the following month, with late payments incurring a 5% monthly surcharge.
  • Phased contribution rates balance employee welfare and employer capacity.
  • Fund provides financial safety net for employees during termination, death, and critical situations.
  • Employers with over ten employees must register unless already providing comparable benefits.
  • Compliance requires accurate contribution calculation, deduction, and remittance.
  • Fund enhances employee rights and financial security, promoting awareness of entitlements.
  • Transition phase until 2030 allows employers to adjust systems and budgets.

posts.title: French Military Influence Shrinks in West Africa Amid Russian Advancements
posts.content:
• Ivory Coast announces French troops’ withdrawal, reducing former colonial influence in West Africa.
  • Senegal confirms closure of French military bases by end of 2025.
  • French forces to withdraw from Ivory Coast’s Port Bouét battalion, transferring control to Ivorian troops.
  • France scaling down military presence across West Africa after troop withdrawals from Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger.
  • France maintains a reduced military presence in Gabon amidst broader African strategy shifts.
  • Increased Russian involvement in Sahel countries following French troop departures.
  • France retains fewer than 2,000 troops in Djibouti and Gabon amid geopolitical recalibration in Africa.
  • Ivory Coast, once a model of stability, faces challenges since 2002 armed rebellion but remains a leading cocoa exporter.

posts.title: Proposed Legislation Targets U.S. Shipbuilding Revival
posts.content:
• Legislation aims to boost U.S. shipbuilding through foreign-built ships.
  • Japanese and South Korean shipyards could benefit from increased U.S. orders starting in 2025.
  • The “SHIPS for America Act of 2024” seeks to grow the U.S. fleet to 250 ships within a decade, focusing on international commerce.

posts.title: Nigeria’s Population Growth Surges Toward 2025
posts.content:
• Nigeria’s population is projected to reach 237,527,782 by 2025.
  • Between 2023 and 2024, the population grew by 4,796,533.
  • Lagos leads with 15,388,000 inhabitants, followed by Kano, Ibadan, Abuja, and Port Harcourt.
  • 53.9% of the population lives in urban areas, totaling 125,447,884 in 2024.
  • Nigeria ranks sixth globally, representing 2.85% of the world’s population.
  • Population density is 255 people per square kilometer with a land area of 910,770 square kilometers.
  • Median age is 17.9 years, and life expectancy is 54.6 years, slightly higher for females than males.
  • Global population expected to reach 8.09 billion by January 1, 2025, with a 2024 increase of over 71 million.

posts.title: India Targets Labor Code Overhaul for 2025 Rollout
posts.content:
• India’s 28 states and 8 union territories aim to finalize draft rules for four labor codes by March 2025.
  • The four labor codes integrate 29 central labor laws, simplifying regulatory compliance.
  • Most states and UTs have completed pre-publication of draft rules, preparing for implementation in 2025.
  • Central and state governments collaborate to harmonize labor rules for uniformity.
  • Objectives include decriminalizing minor offenses, enhancing dispute resolution, and promoting worker welfare.
  • The codes focus on skill development and extending social security to gig and platform workers.
  • Collaboration with ILO includes studying gig economy dynamics to develop tailored social security measures.

posts.title: South Africa: Fuel Prices Adjust Amid Global and Local Pressures
posts.content:
• Petrol prices rise: 93 by 19c, 95 by 12c.
  • Diesel prices increase: 0.05% sulphur by 7c, 0.005% sulphur by 10c.
  • Illuminating paraffin prices drop: wholesale by 9c, retail by 13c.
  • LPGas prices rise by 13c.
  • Coastal petrol prices for 95 ULP increase from R20.68 to R20.80 per litre.
  • Factors include Brent Crude price uptick, OPEC+ decisions, global economic growth concerns, and winter inventory impacts.
  • Rand depreciation against USD drives higher fuel prices.

posts.title: AACCI Advancing Presence in Ethiopia
posts.content:

  • The agreement seeks to strengthen trade relations between Africa and Asia.
  • It prioritizes boosting economic ties, attracting investments, and expanding business opportunities.
  • AACCI will assist Ethiopian businesses in gaining access to Asian markets.
  • The partnership involves knowledge-sharing programs and capacity-building initiatives.
  • The Ethiopian government highlights its commitment to fostering long-term economic growth through international collaborations.

posts.title: India Advances Business Ecosystem with Reforms and Innovation
posts.content:
• Comprehensive regulatory, fiscal, and infrastructure reforms implemented by 2024.
  • Ranked 39th on the Global Innovation Index 2024 among 133 economies.
  • BRAP 2024 initiatives streamline processes using global frameworks like World Bank’s B-READY.
  • Reforms target labor, land administration, taxation, and utility permits.
  • Tax incentives include abolishing “Angel Tax” and reduced corporate taxes for foreign firms.
  • Programs like PM Gati Shakti enhance logistics and digitize property records.
  • Ranked 4th in WIPO’s Science & Technology Cluster Ranking; cities like Mumbai and Bengaluru in top 100 innovation hubs.
  • Strengthened IPR framework with faster patent processing and user-friendly systems.
  • Integration of AI and blockchain improves governance and efficiency.
  • Public-private partnerships foster innovation and infrastructure development.
  • Focus remains on IPR, advanced technologies, and business facilitation.

posts.title: Kariba Dam Safe After Recent Earth Tremor
posts.content:
• The 4.9 magnitude tremor on December 23 did not compromise Kariba Dam’s structural integrity.
  • Multiple tremors this month had epicenters between 10km and 106km from the dam.
  • Inspections confirmed normal dam behavior with no unusual observations.
  • Tremors are typical reservoir-induced events caused by the water load on the earth’s crust.
  • Most tremors in the Kariba area are minor and pose minimal risk.
  • Similar seismic activities have been observed near other large reservoirs globally.

posts.title: Niger Seizes Uranium Mines, Shifts Focus to Russian Investments
posts.content:
• Niger’s government takes control of uranium mines previously managed by French company Orano.
  • The Junta revoked Orano’s mining license, declaring uranium a public domain resource.
  • Relations with France worsen following the military takeover in July 2023.
  • Niger invites Russian companies to invest in uranium and other resources.
  • Orano faces financial losses and production halts amid escalating challenges.
  • New mining laws aim to increase taxes on foreign companies, ensuring better deals for resource exploitation.

posts.title: Asian Markets React to Fiscal Stimulus and Holiday Closures
posts.content:

  • Japan reveals a 115.5 trillion yen budget draft as BOJ hints at rate hikes toward a 2% inflation target.
  • Holiday closures in Indonesia, Hong Kong, Australia, and New Zealand due to Christmas and Boxing Day.
  • U.S. stock index futures steady during light Asian trading, reflecting the Fed’s slower interest rate cut plans for 2025.

posts.title: Ghanaians Vote for New Leadership Amid Economic Challenges
posts.content:
• Presidential election as Nana Akufo-Addo completes two terms.
  • Main contenders: Vice President Mahamudu Bawumia (NPP) and former President John Mahama (NDC).
  • Economic issues include high inflation, unemployment, and COVID-19 impacts.
  • Illegal gold mining remains a contentious environmental issue.
  • Bawumia focuses on economic stabilization; Mahama promises governance reforms and lower taxes.
  • NPP highlights infrastructure and electricity gains; NDC emphasizes past unemployment and press freedom improvements.
  • Over half of Ghana’s population registered to vote; a candidate needs more than 50% to win outright.
  • Analysts expect a peaceful election, maintaining Ghana’s democratic tradition.
  • Citizens hope for a government that addresses economic struggles and fosters progress.

posts.title: Shein Makes a Comeback in India Through Reliance Partnership
posts.content:

  • Competing with Zudio and Myntra in affordable fast fashion.

posts.title: Japan Looks to Asia for Solutions to Worsening Labor Shortages
posts.content:

  • Companies target technical trainees to meet skill demands.
  • Young professionals from Asia play a crucial role in tackling workforce challenges.

posts.title: Africa Investment Forum Spurs $29.5bn in Deals Amid Record Global Interest
posts.content:

  • Record participation: 1,707 investors from 200 institutions across 83 countries.

  • Progress on Italy’s $6bn Mattei Plan to boost infrastructure, energy, healthcare, and education in Africa.

  • Increased global interest: delegations from India, China, Japan; private equity plans to boost Africa allocations.

posts.title: Singapore and South Korea Strengthen Ties with Tourism, Technology, and Investment Boost
posts.content:
• South Korea extends K-ETA exemption for Singaporean travelers until 2025 to boost tourism.
  • In 2023, over 130,000 Singaporeans visited South Korea, while nearly 200,000 South Koreans visited Singapore.
  • South Korea focuses on Singapore’s energy transition technologies, including hydrogen energy for carbon neutrality by 2050.
  • MOUs enhance R&D in renewable energy and sustainable innovation.
  • Collaboration in AI, IoT, robotics, and next-gen vehicles to drive technological advancements.

  • Singapore’s investments in South Korea reached S$112.43 billion in 2023, strengthening economic ties.

  • Joint ventures in semiconductor manufacturing and advanced vehicle technologies.

posts.title: Renovation Push for Liberia’s Capitol Building Sparks Concerns Over Mismanagement and Accountability
posts.content:
• The Capitol Building fire has led to a push for a $1.8 million renovation budget by the Senate, without an investigation or accountability.
  • Historical mismanagement of public building renovations in Liberia, such as the Executive Mansion, raises concerns about fund misuse.
  • There are calls for transparency and a thorough investigation before allocating renovation funds for the Capitol Building.
  • The hasty allocation of funds ignores past financial irregularities and public outcry over mismanaged projects.
  • There is a growing demand for governance reform in Liberia to prioritize accountability and transparency in public spending.

posts.title: Côte d’Ivoire Secures €139.68 Million to Boost Youth Employment and Entrepreneurship
posts.content:
• The African Development Bank approved €139.68 million for youth employment and entrepreneurship in Côte d’Ivoire.
  • A Youth Entrepreneurship Investment Bank (YEIB) will offer financial support, technical assistance, and loan guarantees.
  • Over 8,700 youth, with 50% women, will be trained in sectors like renewable energy, digital economy, and agribusiness.
  • Project aims to create 43,216 direct jobs and 153,094 indirect jobs by 2030, focusing on gender equity.
  • Abidjan’s harbor training center will be renovated to meet international standards.
  • The initiative will enhance agribusiness and align training with market demands through strategic partnerships.

posts.title: Thailand and the UK’s Enhanced Trade Partnership: An Overview
posts.content:
• Agreement covers 20 sectors, including healthcare, clean energy, and digital technology, to boost trade and collaboration.
  • Thailand’s exports to the UK totaled $4.01 billion (2022), and UK’s exports to Thailand were $1.96 billion (2023).
  • Key sectors include automotive (EVs, decarbonization), digital economy (fintech, cybersecurity), healthcare, and agriculture.
  • Promotes low-carbon economies, green finance, and sustainable supply chains.
  • Addresses export compliance costs and strengthens intellectual property enforcement.
  • Aligns with Thailand 4.0 initiative for technology and sustainability.
  • Plans for an EU free trade agreement by 2025 to diversify export markets.

posts.title: Nigerian Govt Bets on Security, Economic Growth with 2025 Budget
posts.content:
• President Bola Tinubu presents a U.S.$31.22 billion Budget for 2025.
  • Titled “Budget of Restoration: Securing Peace, Rebuilding Prosperity.”
  • Priorities include economic growth, human capital development, poverty reduction, and improved security.
  • Significant allocations for the defense, infrastructure, health, and education sectors.
  • Aligns with the government’s Renewed Hope Agenda for sustainable prosperity and economic stability.
  • Under review by the National Assembly for potential amendments.

posts.title: Thailand’s 2025 Global Income Tax: Key Impacts for Residents and Investors
posts.content:
• Thailand plans a tax overhaul by 2025, including taxing residents’ worldwide income and introducing a 15% global minimum corporate tax.
  • Residents spending 180+ days in Thailand would be taxed on global earnings, regardless of income transfer to Thailand, starting 2025.
  • Current tax system taxes foreign income only if brought into Thailand in the same year; proposed changes aim to align with global tax norms.
  • Concerns exist over impact on expatriates, foreign investment, and compliance costs amid these tax reforms.
  • Annual income tax returns must be filed by Thai residents by March, with penalties for non-compliance.
  • New rules effective from 2024 tax all foreign income for Thai residents, regardless of repatriation to Thailand within the year.
  • Proposal also includes a global minimum corporate tax rate of 15% for multinational corporations with high revenues to align with OECD standards.
  • These reforms aim to enhance tax transparency, curb avoidance, and ensure fair contributions from corporations operating in Thailand.

posts.title: India-Serbia Forge Path to €1 Billion Trade with Focus on Defense, IT, and Innovation

  • High-level engagements strengthen bilateral ties.

posts.title: Mali, Niger, and Burkina Faso Plan Historic Exit from Ecowas
posts.content:
• Ecowas approved the withdrawal of Mali, Niger, and Burkina Faso, military-run states, from the bloc, offering a six-month grace period for reconsideration.
  • The three countries, founding members of Ecowas, plan to leave in January after refusing to restore democratic rule.
  • The departure is a major blow to Ecowas, which may lose 76 million people and more than half its land area.
  • The three countries have formed the Alliance of Sahel States (AES) and offer visa-free travel and residency rights for Ecowas citizens.
  • Ecowas hopes for reintegration within six months, but negotiations continue with military juntas who have aligned more with Russia.

posts.title: India Shifts Motor Fuel Exports to Asia as Europe’s Share Declines
posts.content:

  • India’s motor fuel exports were valued at $6.09 billion in the first half of FY25, a 11.76% decline from the previous year.

  • The US, a leading exporter of motor fuel, is expected to increase exports under Trump’s presidency, potentially affecting India’s export opportunities.
  • Europe’s imports of energy products decreased in early 2024, driven by lower consumption and increased renewable energy use.

Manufacturing and processing secured 64.4% of FDI ($20.2 billion), despite […]
posts.content: Vietnam solidified its position as a top FDI destination, attracting $31.4 billion from January to November 2024, a 1% year-on-year rise. Singapore led with $9.14 billion, driven by high-value industries like electronics and energy. South Korea and China followed, with China topping new project numbers. Manufacturing and processing secured 64.4% of FDI ($20.2 billion), despite an 8.7% dip. Real estate surged by 89.1%, attracting $5.63 billion, alongside growth in trade and energy sectors. Key provinces like Bac Ninh and Quang Ninh benefited from significant projects, including Amkor Technology and LG Display expansions. Disbursed FDI reached $21.68 billion (+7.1%), with $318.9 billion of Vietnam’s cumulative $496.7 billion registered FDI realized. Strategic reforms and global partnerships continue to boost Vietnam’s role in global supply chains and regional integration.

posts.title: Egypt to Launch New Gold Exploration Bidding in Q1 2025
posts.excerpt: Egypt’s Ministry of Petroleum, led by Minister Karim Badawi, will launch a new gold and minerals exploration bidding process in early 2025. This announcement followed a meeting with AngloGold Ashanti officials, discussing ongoing operations at the Sukari gold mine, which AngloGold acquired from Centamin. AngloGold plans further investments in exploration and development at Sukari. The […]
posts.content: Egypt’s Ministry of Petroleum, led by Minister Karim Badawi, will launch a new gold and minerals exploration bidding process in early 2025. This announcement followed a meeting with AngloGold Ashanti officials, discussing ongoing operations at the Sukari gold mine, which AngloGold acquired from Centamin. AngloGold plans further investments in exploration and development at Sukari. The meeting also reviewed progress on a mining school, initiated by Centamin, to train local youth, set to open in September 2025. Additionally, a draft agreement for gold exploration between AngloGold and the Egyptian Mineral Resources Authority was signed, pending final approvals. These initiatives align with Egypt’s strategy to enhance its mining sector, attract investments, and solidify its role in the global gold market.

posts.title: Vietnam National Assembly Approves Amendments to 9 Laws: Major Changes to Financial Regulations
posts.excerpt: Vietnam’s National Assembly has introduced critical legislation to accelerate the country’s economic modernization. Key laws passed include the Law on Value-added Tax, the Law on Personal Data Protection, and the Law on Electricity, alongside amendments to nine existing laws, such as the Law on Securities, Accounting, Independent Audit, and Personal Income Tax. Notable changes include […]
posts.content: Vietnam’s National Assembly has introduced critical legislation to accelerate the country’s economic modernization. Key laws passed include the Law on Value-added Tax, the Law on Personal Data Protection, and the Law on Electricity, alongside amendments to nine existing laws, such as the Law on Securities, Accounting, Independent Audit, and Personal Income Tax. Notable changes include improved oversight in securities and auditing, simplified accounting procedures, expanded tax bases for e-commerce, and enhanced public asset management. The State Budget Law now allows local budgets to fund higher-level projects and assist other localities. Updates to the Law on National Reserves empower the Prime Minister to manage reserve goods for foreign relations. Collectively, these measures establish a comprehensive legal framework to support Vietnam’s sustainable economic growth.

posts.title: Amid Opposition, Tax Reform Bills Pass Second Reading At Senate

posts.content: The Nigerian Senate recently passed four tax reform bills for a second reading, sparking debate among lawmakers and stakeholders. The bills aim to simplify taxation, increase VAT allocation to subnational governments, exempt essential goods from VAT, and streamline tax collection processes. Proponents, like Senators Opeyemi Bamidele and Seriake Dickson, see the reforms as a step toward fiscal federalism, while critics, including Senator Ali Ndume, argue that timing and inadequate stakeholder consultation could lead to backlash. Senate Chief Whip Tahir Monguno countered, emphasizing public hearings as the platform for stakeholder input. Despite tensions, the bills advanced, with a public hearing scheduled to address concerns, including VAT derivation. Observers expect further challenges as opposing groups prepare to voice their objections during deliberations.

posts.content: Nigeria’s state-owned refineries, with a combined capacity of 445,000 barrels per day, have underperformed for decades despite over ₦11 trillion spent on rehabilitation since 2010. This inefficiency has forced the country to rely heavily on petroleum imports, draining foreign reserves. The Tinubu administration has announced plans to privatize the refineries in Port Harcourt, Warri, and Kaduna. According to Sunday Dare, special adviser to the president, full privatization is underway to enhance local refining and end fuel queues. Alongside privatization, active contributions from the Dangote and modular refineries aim to meet domestic fuel needs. While the government previously pledged to revive the refineries, timelines for operationalization in 2023 and 2024 were missed. The administration remains focused on achieving self-sufficiency in local refining and reducing dependency on fuel imports.

posts.content: India and South Africa share a deep historical bond shaped by shared struggles against colonialism and apartheid. Their partnership thrives through platforms like BRICS and the IBSA Forum, fostering political and economic collaboration. Bilateral trade grew from $8 billion to $18 billion in five years, driven by coal, minerals, petroleum products, vehicles, and pharmaceuticals. Ongoing negotiations for a trade agreement with the Southern African Customs Union (SACU) promise reduced barriers and enhanced market access. Key sectors include renewable energy, IT, pharmaceuticals, automotive, and food processing. With $70 billion invested across Africa, India’s role is pivotal, complemented by South African investments in India. The Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement simplifies compliance, boosting trade. Initiatives like BRICS and SACU trade agreements are vital for overcoming challenges and strengthening ties further.

posts.content: Addis Abeba—Ethiopia’s Council of Ministers approved a supplementary budget of 581.98 billion birr for the 2024/25 fiscal year, raising the total budget to over 1.5 trillion birr. The increase, equivalent to 56% of the original 971.2 billion birr budget passed in July 2024, addresses projected revenue shortfalls and additional expenditure needs. This supplementary request aligns with Ethiopia’s revised medium-term macroeconomic framework (2024-2028) under the Homegrown Economic Reform agenda. Key reforms, including transitioning to a market-based currency system, have led to increased financial strain, particularly for civil servants. The macroeconomist attributed the request to salary adjustments of up to 332% for 2.4 million public servants, aimed at offsetting rising living costs. Despite the announcement, many employees have yet to see these adjustments reflected in their pay. The proposal awaits final endorsement by parliament.

posts.content: India has intensified ties with CARICOM nations, focusing on trade, healthcare, digital transformation, and cultural exchange. At the 2nd India-CARICOM Summit (Nov 20, 2024), PM Narendra Modi unveiled a 7-pillar action plan emphasizing capacity building, renewable energy, innovation, cricket, maritime security, and healthcare. Key highlights include 1,000 IT scholarships, partnerships in millet cultivation, digital transformation, and maritime security, and adoption of India’s UPI platform. India’s strategic collaboration with Guyana, Trinidad and Tobago, and others has fostered advancements in agriculture, renewable energy, and affordable healthcare. Historical ties through a vibrant Indian diaspora and shared goals in climate action strengthen these relations. CARICOM’s location as a gateway to the Americas and its hydrocarbon reserves align with India’s vision for mutual economic growth and sustainable development.

posts.content: UN Secretary-General António Guterres has called on G20 leaders to tackle global hunger, which affected one in 11 people last year, driven by conflicts, climate change, and economic disparities. South African President Cyril Ramaphosa emphasized the need to eradicate poverty and hunger, advance gender equality, and address climate crises, including biodiversity loss and pollution. The G20 summit coincides with COP29 in Azerbaijan, where progress has stalled over climate finance for developing nations. Both events highlight the urgency of addressing interconnected global challenges, from food insecurity to environmental degradation. Leaders are under pressure to mobilize resources and implement strategies that promote sustainable development, equitable growth, and resilience against climate impacts, ensuring that vulnerable populations and nations are not left behind in the global fight against poverty, hunger, and climate change.

posts.content: The Vietnam-UAE Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), signed on October 28, 2024, marks Vietnam’s first free trade agreement with an Arab nation, enhancing economic ties between the Middle East and ASEAN. Covering 18 chapters, it eliminates tariffs on 98.5-99% of exports, boosting trade in goods like agriculture, seafood, textiles, and electronics. Bilateral trade is expected to reach $10 billion. The CEPA fosters cooperation in tourism, transportation, energy, and financial services while positioning Vietnam as a key destination for UAE investment in high-tech agriculture, manufacturing, and infrastructure. UAE businesses gain access to ASEAN markets, while Vietnam leverages UAE’s trade networks for agricultural and sustainable growth. Strengthening non-oil trade and renewable energy collaboration, the CEPA is set to secure supply chains, promote sustainability, and unlock expansive economic opportunities for both nations.

posts.title: NNPC Refutes Claims of Halting Fuel Imports
posts.excerpt: The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) has refuted claims of ceasing fuel imports, labeling such reports as misleading. Responding to an article quoting its Group CEO, Mele Kyari, the NNPC clarified that his statement about sourcing from domestic refineries was misinterpreted. NNPC prioritizes local refining when cost-effective but remains flexible to import if necessary. […]
posts.content: The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) has refuted claims of ceasing fuel imports, labeling such reports as misleading. Responding to an article quoting its Group CEO, Mele Kyari, the NNPC clarified that his statement about sourcing from domestic refineries was misinterpreted. NNPC prioritizes local refining when cost-effective but remains flexible to import if necessary. The company emphasized that economic viability guides its decisions and that it does not hold exclusive rights to source from local refineries. Additionally, granting import licenses falls under the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA), as per the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA). NNPC highlighted its less-than-30% market share in a deregulated sector, stressing that competition, not mandates, drives efficiency, benefiting consumers through fair pricing and value.

posts.content: Oman’s education sector is rapidly evolving, aligning with Vision 2040 to drive economic diversification and human capital development. With 2,133 schools, 898,073 students, and over 40 higher education institutions, the sector’s contribution to GDP is expected to rise from 4.9% to 6.2% by 2025. Private education, valued at $1.7 billion in 2023, offers substantial growth potential, as only 23% of students currently enroll in private schools, below the GCC average of 30%. Recent reforms, including the School Education Law, prioritize inclusivity, digital transformation, and vocational training. Key opportunities include private schools, special education, online learning, and skills development. With 100% foreign ownership allowed, Oman presents a lucrative landscape for investors to contribute to its education ecosystem and long-term sustainable development.

posts.content: Since 2017, Apple has assembled iPhones in India through suppliers like Foxconn, Tata Electronics, and Pegatron, primarily for entry-level models. However, from 2021, high-end models such as the iPhone 14 and 15 were also produced locally, reflecting Apple’s growing focus on India. Exports from India nearly doubled, reaching $12.1 billion in FY 2023-24, largely due to India’s production-linked incentives (PLI). Foxconn, Tata, and others are expanding facilities, with Tata now managing Wistron’s former operations. India is the third-largest iPhone supplier globally and key for Apple’s diversification beyond China. Notably, Apple’s flagship stores in Mumbai and Delhi cater to its expanding market in India. Future plans include iPhone 17 production in India, with Apple working with new local suppliers to increase its manufacturing footprint.

posts.content: Finance Minister Professor Mthuli Ncube announced that Zimbabwe’s 2025 National Budget will focus on supporting vulnerable groups, including children, women, people with disabilities, and rural communities. Speaking at the Pre-National Budget Seminar in Bulawayo, Prof Ncube emphasized the budget’s alignment with international standards, including health, education, and agriculture allocations. Stakeholders have recommended reducing passport fees, lowering radio licenses, and revising customs duties on essentials to ease costs. The public also urged strengthened social safety nets, timely BEAM disbursements, pension increases, and civil service salary adjustments to address inflation and retain talent. Additionally, calls were made to shorten duty-free vehicle import periods for civil servants and fill critical vacancies in healthcare and education, especially in rural areas.

posts.content: Nigeria’s Minister of Information, Mohammed Idris, emphasized at the Arab-Islamic Summit in Riyadh that Nigeria advocates for a peaceful resolution to the Israel-Palestine conflict, warning it cannot be resolved militarily. With a longstanding connection to the Middle East, Nigeria is leveraging this summit to promote diplomatic solutions and an immediate ceasefire. President Tinubu is expected to echo Nigeria’s stance on the two-state solution, urging coexistence with secure borders for both Israel and Palestine. Idris cautioned that without peace, regional instability could escalate globally, affecting nations like Nigeria.

By mandating transparent bidding and removing pre-arranged bid risks, the decree aims to increase competition and attract investors. Key provisions include prerequisites for land bidding, […]
posts.content: Decree 115/2024, effective September 16, 2024, sets a clear framework for investor selection in land-use projects in Vietnam, focusing on competitive bidding in the energy sector, particularly greenfield power projects. By mandating transparent bidding and removing pre-arranged bid risks, the decree aims to increase competition and attract investors. Key provisions include prerequisites for land bidding, streamlined investor selection processes, incentives for environmentally friendly technologies, and updated scoring criteria. It also regulates project transfer rules and mandates competitive bidding for renewable power projects if multiple investors are interested. Decree 115 aligns with Vietnam’s broader legal framework, including the Law on Electricity, aiming to foster foreign investment, advance energy infrastructure, and support sustainable development.

posts.content: Pinnacle Oil & Gas signed a 13-year Interconnection Agreement with Dangote Refinery, using its $1 billion Petrol Terminal to improve petroleum distribution across Nigeria. CEO Robert Dickerman emphasized their investment in pipelines for cost-effective distribution, reducing reliance on ships and trucks. Dangote supported the project by facilitating regulatory approval, aiming for a market-based solution to Nigeria’s energy needs. Dickerman noted that efficient distribution relies on competitive pricing and quality products, regardless of origin. Pinnacle’s Lekki terminal, operational since 2021, minimizes costs by eliminating the need for ship-to-ship transfers, improving efficiency. Responding to Dangote’s recent statement, he clarified that imports don’t imply substandard quality, as the regulator ensures standards. Pinnacle anticipates that Dangote’s integration into Nigeria’s distribution network will enhance industry stability and encourage investment in refining and storage.

posts.content: India’s investments in the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) have surged, focusing on energy, diamonds, and gold. Established in 1991, the CIS links ex-USSR countries, excluding the Baltic states, and provides a resource-rich trade zone between Asia and Europe. India’s “Focus CIS Programme” and initiatives like the International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC) enhance connectivity and market access. Key partnerships include energy imports from Azerbaijan and Kazakhstan, defense and energy collaboration with Russia, and pharmaceuticals and infrastructure with Tajikistan and Turkmenistan. India also works with Belarus on potash fertilizers and Georgia in cultural and economic exchanges. Efforts are supported by trade forums and agreements with the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU), as well as bilateral mechanisms like the India-Central Asia Dialogue, advancing India’s trade growth and strategic engagement across the CIS.

posts.content: Aliko Dangote, Nigerian oil billionaire, has questioned why the state-owned Nigeria National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) and private retailers continue to import petroleum when his refinery has over 500 million liters in stock, claiming it’s sufficient for Nigeria if retailers purchase from it. Despite this, analysts express doubts about whether this supply can fully meet Nigeria’s demand. Recently, Dangote’s company, the Dangote Group, has clashed with the NNPC and private oil firms over control of the domestic petroleum market.

International treaties like the WTO, CPTPP, and ASEAN agreements may provide favorable terms, though compliance with investment laws, […]
posts.content: Vietnam is an attractive destination for foreign investment, particularly in manufacturing, technology, and infrastructure. However, foreign investors must adhere to regulations, avoiding prohibited business lines and meeting market access conditions per Vietnam’s Foreign Investor Market Access List. International treaties like the WTO, CPTPP, and ASEAN agreements may provide favorable terms, though compliance with investment laws, such as Decree 31/2021, remains essential. Additionally, stringent guidelines apply to insurance, workforce recruitment, and equipment imports, as outlined in specific decrees. Foreign workers require permits, while used equipment imports must meet Vietnam’s standards and may need approval if exceeding age limits. Vietnam’s investment laws protect against expropriation, promising fair compensation for assets seized under national security or emergency grounds, offering foreign investors a more secure landscape.

posts.content: Commonwealth leaders are convening this week in Samoa, where discussions include Africa’s potential to secure the Secretary-General role after a 20-year gap. Three African candidates are in the running: Ghana’s Foreign Minister Shirley Ayorkor Botchwey, Lesotho’s former trade minister Joshua Phoho Setipa, and Gambia’s Foreign Minister Mamadou Tangara. Controversy surrounds whether reparations should be on the agenda, raising debates within the association. Rwanda is also pushing for the 56-member group to intensify efforts in eliminating barriers that hinder women’s and girls’ advancement, highlighting ongoing gender equity challenges. This gathering underscores the Commonwealth’s broader objectives, balancing historical legacies with contemporary priorities in social and economic equity.

posts.content: India and Türkiye share a multifaceted relationship, marked by both diplomatic challenges and economic collaboration. Political tensions, notably Türkiye’s defense ties with Pakistan, have affected diplomatic engagement, with India’s focus shifting to trade and economic partnerships outside of defense. In 2024, the two nations signed an Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) MoU to streamline cross-border investments and facilitate trade, despite declining bilateral trade figures. Indian and Turkish companies are active in each other’s markets across sectors like construction, automotive, and technology. Türkiye’s new Tech Visa Program also attracts Indian professionals to its tech industry. While Türkiye’s BRICS aspirations and India’s strategic stance shape future dynamics, initiatives in trade, tourism, and joint investments signal strong potential for resilient bilateral growth despite geopolitical complexities.

posts.content: The upcoming 21st replenishment (IDA21) of the World Bank’s International Development Association (IDA), set for December 2024, has drawn significant attention. IDA offers favorable terms but is only accessible to countries with per capita incomes below $1,315. World Bank President Ajay Banga has urged donors to contribute $28-30 billion, which could be leveraged to raise up to $100 billion in capital markets. African leaders are calling for the total amount to reach $120 billion. In comparison, $23.5 billion was pledged during IDA20 in 2021, with a record $26 billion in 2012. So far, Denmark is the only donor to pre-announce its contribution, pledging $492 million, a 40% increase over its 2021 contribution.

posts.content: Indonesia, Southeast Asia’s largest economy, offers vast opportunities for Indian businesses, particularly in agriculture, poultry, food processing, and technology. With a large labor force in agriculture and rising domestic demand, Indian firms can introduce agri-tech solutions, export seeds and fertilizers, and form agribusiness partnerships. In the poultry sector, modernization and supply chain enhancements offer investment prospects, while food processing, driven by urbanization, presents growth potential in halal products and packaging. Indonesia’s booming digital economy, projected to reach US$130 billion by 2025, also attracts Indian fintech, tech, and start-up collaborations. Favorable government policies, including SEZ incentives and the Omnibus Law, further boost investment. With strong bilateral ties and increasing trade, Indian businesses are well-positioned to thrive in Indonesia’s dynamic market.

posts.content: Benin has pledged $2 million to the African Development Fund (ADF) during the Mid-Term Review of the 16th Replenishment in Cotonou. The ADF, part of the African Development Bank Group, provides grants and low-interest loans to support low-income African countries. Benin’s Minister of Economy and Finance, Romuald Wadagni, emphasized the ADF’s role as a trusted partner for development, urging transparency and rigour from recipient countries. Benin joins six other African contributors, including Algeria, Angola, Egypt, and South Africa. The current three-year ADF financing cycle, ending in 2025, received a record $8.9 billion in donations. Wadagni highlighted Benin’s goal of leveraging ADF guarantees to raise additional funds for development projects. The ADF has benefited 74 million people, particularly in agriculture.

posts.content: India and Denmark share a strong, longstanding relationship, bolstered by collaborations in political, economic, and research fields. Denmark has invested US$1.81 billion in sectors like renewable energy, shipping, and engineering, while Indian IT companies like Infosys have expanded in Denmark. Recent collaborations include Infosys modernizing TDC Net’s IT systems and Rockwool’s expansion in India. Novo Nordisk is strengthening its presence in India, focusing on pharmaceutical R&D and AI integration. The India-Denmark Energy Partnership (INDEP) further enhances cooperation in offshore wind and renewable energy, positioning both nations for a sustainable future.

posts.content: Sudan’s Minister of Finance, Dr. Gibril Ibrahim, is leading the country’s delegation to the 2024 annual meetings of the IMF and World Bank in Washington from October 21-26. The meetings focus on the Development Committee, International Monetary Committee, and Finance Committee sessions. The Sudanese delegation, including Undersecretary Mohamed Bashar Mohamed and a technical team, aims to address external debt and secure financing for health, education, and humanitarian projects through international organizations. Dr. Ibrahim is also scheduled to hold bilateral meetings with representatives from the IMF, World Bank, and regional financial institutions, as well as counterparts from other countries, to strengthen economic cooperation and deepen ties with bilateral partners.

posts.content: India is emerging as a hub for climate-friendly business models, attracting global capital, according to Srini Nagarajan, Managing Director at British International Investment (BII). BII, with a $2.3 billion portfolio in India, has committed over $1 billion between 2022 and 2026, focusing on renewable energy, battery storage, biofuels, and cooling solutions. BII has invested in companies like Ayana Renewable Power, Fourth Partner Energy, and Mahindra’s electric vehicle unit. Nagarajan emphasized that BII’s role is to create bankable opportunities and attract commercial investors. The institution also backs venture capital funds in sectors like climate tech, healthcare, and food & agri. BII is keen on supporting India’s underfunded transmission sector and infrastructure investment trusts (InvITs), providing risk-tolerant capital to encourage retail and commercial investment.

Egypt has lost $6-7 billion over the past 10 months due to regional and global repercussions. He also praised Egypt’s achievements in eliminating Hepatitis C and malaria, positioning the country as a global health success. Despite economic instability since 2011, Sisi noted progress in reducing unemployment to 6.5%, thanks to extensive infrastructure development and reforms aimed at providing millions of job opportunities annually.

posts.content: India and Ireland are in advanced talks to establish a joint economic commission by 2024, aiming to strengthen trade and economic relations. With bilateral trade reaching $6.38 billion in 2023-24, the two countries are building on a decade of growth in both goods and services trade. Ireland views India as a key partner in the Asia-Pacific, highlighted during Foreign Secretary Joe Hackett’s visit to New Delhi in 2024. India’s growing economic influence and a large Indian community in Ireland are driving deeper political, economic, and cultural ties. Ireland’s focus on sectors like IT, fintech, med-tech, clean energy, and education aligns with India’s expanding markets, presenting significant opportunities for collaboration. Multilateral cooperation at the UN and future partnerships in AI and renewable energy further solidify this evolving relationship.

posts.content: Vietnam’s Digital Infrastructure Strategy by 2025, with a Vision to 2030, focuses on nationwide 5G deployment, achieving 99% coverage by 2030, and building robust data infrastructure, including undersea fiber optic cables and green data centers. By 2025, the country aims for two international cables and by 2030, six, along with hyperscale data centers. The strategy targets key sectors like smart transportation, healthcare, education, and tourism, with IoT adoption growing from one connection per citizen in 2025 to four by 2030. Digital signatures will rise from 50% to 70% adoption. Vietnam aims to become a top 50 global player in e-government and digital economy, enhancing its competitiveness and attracting foreign investment in cutting-edge technologies.

posts.content: Starting April 1, 2023, all companies in India, including Section 8 companies, must maintain an audit trail in their accounting software. This requirement ensures that every transaction is recorded with a time-stamped, tamper-proof edit log. Auditors must verify that the audit trail was enabled throughout the financial year, protected from tampering, and compliant with statutory retention rules. Non-compliance can result in fines between INR 50,000 and INR 500,000 for companies, directors, CFOs, and auditors. In severe cases, imprisonment or professional disqualification may occur. Companies are urged to ensure their software providers support audit trail features and to collaborate with auditors for seamless compliance, safeguarding transparency and accountability.

Focused on the theme “Harnessing Science, Technology, and Innovation (STI) for a more peaceful and sustainable future,” the assembly, which began on October 13, 2024, brings together global parliamentary representatives. The Somali delegates will engage in discussions on the role of STI in addressing climate change, conflict resolution, and sustainable development. This participation highlights Somalia’s commitment to using technology for domestic growth and global peace initiatives. The event also offers opportunities for international networking, potentially enhancing Somalia’s bilateral and multilateral collaborations. Insights gained at the assembly may inform future policies in Somalia, aligning scientific advancements with sustainable development goals.

posts.content: The bilateral relationship between Norway and India is poised for growth, particularly in renewable energy, maritime technologies, and sustainable development. The 2024 Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA) between India and the EFTA (including Norway) eliminates tariffs on most Norwegian exports, boosting trade and creating new opportunities in sectors like health tech and green mobility. Norway’s expertise in maritime and clean technologies aligns with India’s growing needs, fostering collaboration in shipbuilding, renewable energy, and environmental solutions. The upcoming India-Nordic Summit in 2024 will further strengthen ties in trade, investment, and sustainability. Norway’s commitment to leveraging India’s skilled workforce, particularly in IT and healthcare, enhances its global competitiveness, while the modernization of the India-Norway Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (DTAA) aims to facilitate smoother cross-border business operations.

Indian companies, including Apollo Tyres and HCL Technologies, are key investors in Hungary, providing over 10,000 jobs. Institutional mechanisms, such as the Joint Committee on Economic Cooperation, continue to facilitate bilateral relations, which are focused on trade, investment, and sustainable growth.

posts.content: Liberia’s mining sector has praised President Joseph N. Boakai for signing Executive Order No. 136, establishing the National Railway Authority (NRA) to oversee the country’s rail infrastructure. The NRA will ensure efficient, transparent, and equitable access to Liberia’s rail assets, supporting multi-user infrastructure and promoting economic development. HPX, an American mining company, welcomed the move, emphasizing its role in facilitating iron ore shipments from Guinea via Liberia’s Yekepa-Buchanan line. The Liberia Chamber of Mines also commended the decision, highlighting the positive impact on mineral transport, foreign investment, and job creation. Executive Order No. 136 expands on previous commitments to improve Liberia’s rail network and includes funding mechanisms through user fees and arbitration for disputes. The NRA is seen as a critical step in advancing Liberia’s infrastructure and economic growth.

posts.content: India and Australia have deepened their bilateral relationship, evolving from a Strategic Partnership in 2009 to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership (CSP) in 2020. Economic ties have strengthened, with the Australia-India Economic Cooperation and Trade Agreement (ECTA) facilitating tariff-free trade for most goods, and negotiations for a Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Agreement (CECA) underway. Both nations are collaborating in critical minerals, renewable energy, and education. Notable investments, such as Australia’s Deakin University campus in India, highlight growing opportunities. Bilateral trade reached US$31.4 billion in 2022, with key exports in minerals, technology, and education. Continued efforts in defense, trade, and people-to-people ties are set to drive further economic growth and regional stability.

posts.content: The General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) hosted a delegation of 24 Japanese companies in the renewable energy sector to discuss the development and localization of green energy technology. GAFI CEO Hossam Heiba stated that the government has identified sites and investment needs to achieve an additional 30 megawatts of renewable energy. Several companies have already begun investing to support Egypt’s renewable energy goals. The meeting was attended by key representatives from the Japan External Trade Organization (JETRO), Japan Bank for International Cooperation (JBIC), and Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA). GAFI aims not only to boost renewable energy production but also to localize the technology for turbines and panels used in solar and wind power plants, further enhancing Egypt’s industrial and trade capabilities in this vital sector.

posts.content: Egypt is implementing key tax reforms to foster a more business-friendly environment, particularly for small and international companies. Recent announcements (Sept 11-12, 2024) include a simplified tax regime for businesses with annual turnovers up to EGP 15 million, targeting small enterprises and freelancers. This initiative promotes compliance by allowing tax return submissions for 2021-2023 without penalties. For international companies, the threshold for transfer pricing studies has been raised to EGP 30 million, easing compliance for smaller firms. Additional measures streamline tax administration, including a risk management system, reduced penalties, and improved VAT refunds. These reforms aim to enhance revenue collection, attract foreign investment, and support Egypt’s economic recovery, positioning the country for sustained growth

posts.content: The Middle East and Africa (MEA) region saw a 10.4% decline in deal activity in the first eight months of 2024, reflecting global economic caution, as reported by GlobalData. Globally, deal activity dropped 15%, with mergers and acquisitions (M&A), private equity, and venture financing facing significant downturns due to macroeconomic and geopolitical challenges. North America saw the steepest decline at 18.9%, while India and Japan defied the trend with improved activity. Despite the slowdown, the downturn presents opportunities for investors to acquire undervalued assets and position themselves for future growth, particularly in the MEA region. Strategic foresight and adaptability will be key for those looking to capitalize on the eventual market recovery and long-term value creation.

posts.content: India and Finland have enjoyed strong diplomatic ties since 1949, evolving into a robust partnership in trade, technology, and innovation. Recent engagements, such as the DESI framework, focus on education, innovation, and renewable energy. Finland’s expertise in AI, telecommunications, and nuclear energy aligns with India’s technological and green energy goals. Trade between the two countries amounts to €1.5–2 billion annually, with Finnish companies excelling in telecommunications and clean energy, while Indian IT firms make their mark in Finland. Moving forward, both nations aim to enhance cooperation in quantum computing, vocational training, and climate action, building a sustainable and innovative future.

posts.content: In 2024, Southeast Asia’s manufacturing sector is shaped by evolving economic conditions and strategic investments. Vietnam and Thailand show moderate growth with PMIs of 52.4 and 52, bolstered by infrastructure improvements and strong export sectors. Indonesia and Cambodia face contraction (PMIs of 48.9), impacted by supply chain disruptions and external demand pressures. Malaysia’s sector stagnates (PMI 49.7), but government incentives target high-tech manufacturing. The Philippines sees modest growth (PMI 51.2), focusing on semiconductors and foreign investments. Singapore (PMI 50.9) remains competitive in biotech and electronics despite high labor costs. Across the region, policies aim to stimulate investment, diversify manufacturing bases, and enhance global trade connectivity.
